docs.title: 13.1. Installing Node.js
docs.text:
[Node.js] can be downloaded from nodejs.org: choose version LTS (long-term support) 24, or version 22 starting with 22.22.3: these are the versions required by [Angular] 22. The [Windows] installer also installs [npm]. Verify the installation in a console:

node --version
npm --version

To run multiple versions of [Node.js] on the same machine, you can use [nvm-windows] (under [Windows]) or [nvm] (under [Linux] and [macOS]).

The examples and case study do not require the installation of any global tools: [Angular CLI] (the [ng] command), the [Angular] compiler, [TypeScript] (and, for the server, the [nest] tool) are part of each project’s dependencies, installed by [npm install]. The scripts in [package.json] ([npm start], [npm run build]) are located in the [node_modules] folder. To create a new project yourself, you can use [npx @angular/cli new mon-projet] without installing anything.

docs.title: 13.2. Installing Visual Studio Code
docs.text:
[Visual Studio Code] can be downloaded from code.visualstudio.com. For [Angular], install the Angular Language Service extension (Angular editor) from the Extensions panel (Ctrl+Shift+X): code completion and type checking in templates, navigation from a selector ([<app-champ-saisie>]) to the component class, from a [templateUrl] to the template file, and real-time highlighting of [Angular] compiler errors as you type.

Open a project via the File / Open Folder menu (the [exemples-angular] folder, for example), and open a console within it via the Terminal / New Terminal menu.

docs.title: 13.3. The Angular DevTools extension
docs.text:
The Angular extension DevTools can be installed from the extension store in [Chrome], [Edge], or [Firefox]. It adds an “Angular” tab to the browser’s developer tools (F12), which displays the following for an application running in development mode:

  • the page’s component tree, and, for each component, its inputs, outputs, and properties (signals and their values);
  • a component’s signal graph: which [computed] depends on which signal;
  • the injected services and the injector tree;
  • the router’s routes;
  • a profiler, which measures the time spent updating each component.

You can modify a piece of data there and watch the page update: an excellent way to understand responsiveness.

docs.title: 13.4. Installing MySQL with Laragon
docs.text:
The JSON server requires [MySQL] (or [MariaDB]). [Laragon] (laragon.org) installs one under [Windows], ready to use, with the [HeidiSQL] administration tool. After installation:

  • the “Start All” button launches the [MySQL] server on port 3306;
  • the user [root] has no password: these are the default values from the server’s [.env.example] file;
  • in [HeidiSQL] (the “Database” button), the File / Run SQL menu item runs the [database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql] script.

In [Linux] or [macOS], install [MySQL] or [MariaDB] using the system’s package manager, and run the script using the command-line client: [mysql -u root -p < database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql].

docs.title: 13.5. Installing curl
docs.text:
[curl] is included with [Windows] versions 10 and 11, [macOS], and most distributions of [Linux]. Check its version:

curl --version

The option [--json], used in this document, has been available since version 7.82 (2022). If you are using an older version, replace [--json @fichier] with [-H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @fichier], or install a recent version starting with curl.se.

In [PowerShell], you must enter [curl.exe], not [curl]: In [PowerShell], [curl] is an alias for another command ([Invoke-WebRequest]), which does not include the options from [curl]. The command prompt ([cmd]) does not have this issue.

docs.title: 10. Case Study: The Angular client for the RdvMedecins application
10.1. The Problem
docs.text:
The [RdvMedecins] application allows users to schedule appointments at a doctor’s office. The [NestJS] course wrote it as a HTML application, in which the server generated the pages. Here we are writing the client [Angular]: the MÊMES pages, generated in the browser from the JSON data on the server described in the chapter “The RdvMedecins Server: A Black Box.”

The client must provide everything that the HTML application provided:

  • a login page, protected by a CAPTCHA, with the option to create a patient account;
  • a doctor’s schedule for a given day, with appointment booking (patient selection window) and cancellation;
  • for the administrator, management of doctors and clients (list, add, edit, delete);
  • for the patient, a personal dashboard (showing upcoming appointments, which they can cancel) and account management;
  • two languages: French and English;
  • unique URLs ([/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=...]), which can be reloaded, bookmarked, and navigated using the browser’s Back/Forward buttons.

docs.title: 10.2. Installation and Execution
docs.text:
The JSON server must be installed and running (see the chapter “The RdvMedecins Server: A Black Box”). To use the client in a browser, you do not need the CAPTCHA test mode: you can leave the [CAPTCHA_TEST] field blank in the [.env] file on the server.

In a console window open to the [rdvmedecins-angular] folder:

npm install
npm start

then open http://localhost:4200 in a browser. The demo accounts are listed on the login page (password = login).

The examples also use port 4200: first, stop the currently running example ([Ctrl-C]). You can also start the client on a different port: [npm start -- --port 4300].

docs.title: 10.4. Client architecture
docs.text:
rdvmedecins-angular/
├── angular.json, package.json, tsconfig.json, proxy.conf.json
├── public/favicon.svg                l'icône de l'onglet
└── src/
    ├── index.html                    LA page de l'application
    ├── main.ts                       le démarrage
    ├── styles.css
    └── app/
        ├── app.config.ts             la configuration de l'application
        ├── app.ts                    le gabarit commun à toutes les pages
        ├── app.routes.ts             les pages et leurs droits d'accès
        ├── gardes.ts                 les gardes du routeur
        ├── api/                      la couche d'accès à l'API
        ├── i18n/                     les langues
        ├── services/                 session, messages, confirmation, formulaires
        ├── pipes/                    la mise en forme
        ├── components/               les composants réutilisables
        └── pages/                    les pages

The following table compares the HTML application from the [NestJS] course with this client:

Application HTML (NestJS)Angular clientThe server generates each page ([res.render])The server returns JSON; the components of [src/app/pages/] generate the pages[views/layout.hbs] and its partial views[app.ts] and the components of [src/app/components/]the controller routes ([@Get('agenda')])client routes ([app.routes.ts]); the server only has /api/... routes[JwtAuthGuard] and [RolesGuard] redirect to /login or a 403 pagerouter guards; the server maintains its own guards, which return 401 or 403flash message in a cookieflash message in a service, [MessagesService]dictionaries read by the server, helper [{{t}}]dictionaries in the client, [ngx-translate]; the server returns only keyslanguage stored in a cookielanguage stored in the [localStorage]form rejected: the server reloads the pageform rejected: 400/409 response; the client displays the errors below the fieldsConfirmation window: a small script, [public/js/app.js]a service and a component, [FenetreConfirmation]The application works without JavaScriptThe EST application from JavaScript

The client [Vue.js] from the previous lesson has exactly the same structure: the “stores” ([Pinia]) have become services, the “composables” have become services or functions, and the views have become pages.

All of the client’s files are shown below. They are extensively commented; these comments are part of the course.

// =========================================================================
// main.ts - Application startup
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The root component (App) and the application configuration
// (app.config.ts). The style sheets (Bootstrap, styles.css) are
// declared in angular.json.
// =========================================================================

import { bootstrapApplication } from '@angular/platform-browser';
import { App } from './app/app';
import { appConfig } from './app/app.config';

bootstrapApplication(App, appConfig).catch((erreur) => console.error(erreur));

docs.title: 10.4.2.3. src/app/app.config.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// app.config.ts - the application configuration
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
//    - the router, its routes (app.routes.ts), and the route parameters
//      sent to page URLs, and the translated tab titles;
//    - HttpClient, with the error and 401 interceptor;
//    - ngx-translate (French and English).
// =========================================================================

import { ApplicationConfig, provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners } from '@angular/core';
import { provideHttpClient, withInterceptors } from '@angular/common/http';
import { provideRouter, TitleStrategy, withComponentInputBinding } from '@angular/router';
import { routes } from './app.routes';
import { apiInterceptor } from './api/api.interceptor';
import { provideI18n } from './i18n/i18n';
import { TitreTraduit } from './i18n/titre.strategy';

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
     // unhandled errors are reported in the browser console
    provideBrowserGlobalErrorListeners(),
    provideRouter(routes, withComponentInputBinding()),
    { provide: TitleStrategy, useClass: TitreTraduit },
    provideHttpClient(withInterceptors([apiInterceptor])),
    provideI18n(),
  ],
};
  • line 21: unhandled errors (such as a rejected promise that no one is waiting for) are reported in the browser console;
  • line 22: the router, with the route parameters passed to the page inputs (example 17);
  • Line 23: [TitleStrategy] is the router service that sets the tab title for each browsing session. We replace the one from [Angular] with our own ([i18n/titre.strategy.ts]), which translates the title. This is the whole point of dependency injection: you can substitute your own class for the framework’s class without changing anything else;
  • line 24: the HTTP client, with our interceptor;
  • line 25: [ngx-translate].

// =========================================================================
// app.ts - the root component: GABARIT, common to all pages
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The equivalent of views/layout.hbs in the HTML application:
//    - the navigation bar;
//    - a success message in HAUT;
//    - the current page (<router-outlet>);
//    - the error area in BAS;
//    - the confirmation window, displayed once for the entire application.
// =========================================================================

import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { RouterOutlet } from '@angular/router';
import { BarreNavigation } from './components/barre-navigation/barre-navigation';
import { MessageSucces } from './components/message-succes';
import { ZoneErreur } from './components/zone-erreur';
import { FenetreConfirmation } from './components/fenetre-confirmation/fenetre-confirmation';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  imports: [RouterOutlet, BarreNavigation, MessageSucces, ZoneErreur, FenetreConfirmation],
  template: `
    <div class="container py-4">
      <app-barre-navigation />
      <app-message-succes />
      <router-outlet />
      <app-zone-erreur />
    </div>
    <app-fenetre-confirmation />
  `,
})
export class App {}
  • Lines 22–30: the template common to all pages: the navigation bar, the success message, the current page, the error area, and the confirmation window (Example 16).

.zone-erreur {
  position: sticky;
  bottom: 1rem;
  z-index: 1060;
  pointer-events: none;
  margin-top: 1.5rem;
  padding: 0.75rem 1rem;
  background-color: #fdecef; /* light pink */

  border-radius: 0.375rem;
  color: #842029;

// =========================================================================
// api/types.ts - the JSON objects exchanged with the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The translation, into TypeScript interfaces, of the API described in chapter
// "The Server, a Black Box." The compiler thus verifies that the client
// uses only fields that actually exist.
// =========================================================================

export type Role = 'ADMIN' | 'DOCTOR' | 'USER';

// POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/me, PUT /api/my-account
export interface Utilisateur {
  login: string;
  nom: string; // display name: "Marie PELISSIER"
  role: Role;
}

// GET /api/captcha
export interface Captcha {
  id: string;
  svg: string;
}

// a title, a first name, a last name
export interface Identite {
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
}

// a doctor or a client: GET /api/doctors, GET /api/clients/:id...
export interface Personne extends Identite {
  id: number;
  version: number; // optimistic lock: to be sent back with a modification
  login?: string; // only for ADMIN
}

// what is sent to create/modify a person (ADMIN)
export interface DonneesPersonne extends Identite {
  login: string; // '' = default value (creation) or unchanged (modification)
  password: string; // same as above
  version?: number;
}

export interface Creneau {
  id: number;
  hdebut: number;
  mdebut: number;
  hfin: number;
  mfin: number;
}

// an entry in the calendar, with the DROITS for the logged-in user
export interface CreneauAgenda extends Creneau {
  libre: boolean;
  patient: Identite | null; // null: available, or occupied by another patient
  moi: boolean; // the logged-in patient’s appointment
  reservable: boolean;
  idRv: number | null; // indicates whether the user can cancel
}

// GET /api/agenda?idMedecin=...&day=...
export interface Agenda {
  medecin: Personne;
  jour: string; // "yyyy-MM-dd"
  creneaux: CreneauAgenda[];
  info: string | null; // translation key (patient who already has an appointment)
}

// GET /api/my-account
export interface MonEspace {
  patient: Identite;
  rendezVous: { id: number; jour: string; creneau: Creneau; medecin: Personne }[];
}

// GET /api/my-account
export interface MonCompte extends Identite {
  login: string;
  version: number;
}

// PUT /api/my-account
export interface ModificationMonCompte extends Identite {
  login: string;
  password: string; // '' = unchanged
  confirmation: string;
  motDePasseActuel: string;
  version: number;
}

// POST /api/registration
export interface Inscription extends Identite {
  login: string;
  password: string;
  confirmation: string;
}

The translation into [TypeScript] interfaces of the API described in the chapter “The RdvMedecins server, a black box.” The keyword [extends] avoids repeating common fields: a [Personne] is a [Identite] (title, first name, last name) with an identifier and a version.

// =========================================================================
// api/erreur-api.ts - UNE class for all errors in API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Reuse of common/erreur-api.ts examples. Any request error
// (4xx/5xx server response, server unreachable, proxy response)
// becomes a ErreurApi, which contains the CLÉ message translation, its
// parameters, and the error for each field in a rejected form.
// =========================================================================

import { HttpErrorResponse } from '@angular/common/http';

export class ErreurApi extends Error {
  constructor(
    public readonly statusCode: number, // 0: the server did not respond
    public readonly cle: string, // translation key: 'ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN'
    public readonly params: Record<string, string> = {},
    public readonly champs: Record<string, string> = {}, // error in each field
  ) {
    super(cle);
    this.name = 'ErreurApi';
  }
}

export function versErreurApi(e: unknown): ErreurApi {
  if (e instanceof ErreurApi) {
    return e;
  }
  if (!(e instanceof HttpErrorResponse)) {
    return new ErreurApi(0, 'ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR');
  }
  const corps = (typeof e.error === 'object' && e.error !== null ? e.error : {}) as {
    cle?: string;
    params?: Record<string, string>;
    champs?: Record<string, string>;
  };
  return new ErreurApi(
    e.status,
     // No key: the response did not come from our server, but from the network
     // or a proxy (ng serve: 500 with no body; nginx: 502, 504...)
    corps.cle ?? (e.status === 0 || e.status >= 500 ? 'ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE' : 'ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR'),
    corps.params,
    corps.champs,
  );
}

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// api/api.interceptor.ts - the interceptor for TOUTES requests to API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from the examples in commun/erreurs.interceptor.ts, with a new feature:
// Centralized handling of the 401 response.
//
// A 401 can occur at any time: the token has expired (2 hours), the
// the account has been deleted, the server has restarted with a different secret key
// secret key... Rather than handling this case in each component, we
// handle it once in ICI: we forget the user, prepare the
// "session expired" message, and redirect to the login page.
//
// Some requests handle their own 401 errors (login, GET
// /api/auth/moi...): they signal this with a JETON DE CONTEXTE
// (HttpContextToken), a piece of information attached to the request, which
// is read by the interceptor (see api/rdvmedecins.api.ts).
// =========================================================================

import { inject } from '@angular/core';
import { HttpContextToken, HttpInterceptorFn } from '@angular/common/http';
import { Router } from '@angular/router';
import { catchError, throwError } from 'rxjs';
import { versErreurApi } from './erreur-api';
import { SessionService } from '../services/session.service';
import { MessagesService } from '../services/messages.service';

// true: the request handles any 401 responses itself (default is false)
export const IGNORER_401 = new HttpContextToken<boolean>(() => false);

export const apiInterceptor: HttpInterceptorFn = (req, next) => {
   // inject: the services that will be needed (in the context of injection
   // by the interceptor, AVANT sending the request)
  const session = inject(SessionService);
  const messages = inject(MessagesService);
  const router = inject(Router);

  return next(req).pipe(
    catchError((e: unknown) => {
      const erreur = versErreurApi(e);
      if (erreur.statusCode === 401 && !req.context.get(IGNORER_401)) {
        session.oublier();
        messages.flash('erreur', 'ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED');
        router.navigate(['/login']);
      }
      return throwError(() => erreur);
    }),
  );
};

The interceptor from Example 24, with a new feature: centralized handling of the 401 response. A 401 can occur at any time: the token has expired, the account has been deleted... Rather than handling this case on every page, we handle it here, once.

  • Line 28: a context token ([HttpContextToken])—information attached to a request that the interceptor can read. By default, this is set to [false];
  • Lines 33–35: The interceptor injects the services it will need. [inject] must be called at the beginning of the function: later, in [catchError], the injection context no longer exists;
  • line 39: any error becomes a [ErreurApi];
  • lines 40–44: a 401 response for a request that does not handle it itself: the user is ignored, the “session expired” message is prepared (it will be displayed on the next page), and the user is redirected to the login page;
  • line 45: the error is passed, in all cases, to the code that made the request.

docs.title: 10.4.3.4. src/app/api/rdvmedecins.api.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// api/rdvmedecins.api.ts - one method per route in API
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The client’s “data access layer”: components call these
// methods, which are typed, without knowing anything about URL, HttpClient, or JSON. If
// the API changes, only this file changes.
// Each method returns a PROMESSE (firstValueFrom): the components
// chain requests using async/await. In case of failure, the promise
// is rejected with a ErreurApi (see api.interceptor.ts).
// =========================================================================

import { inject, Injectable } from '@angular/core';
import { HttpClient, HttpContext, HttpParams } from '@angular/common/http';
import { firstValueFrom } from 'rxjs';
import { IGNORER_401 } from './api.interceptor';
import {
  Agenda,
  Captcha,
  DonneesPersonne,
  Inscription,
  ModificationMonCompte,
  MonCompte,
  MonEspace,
  Personne,
  Utilisateur,
} from './types';

// /api/doctors or /api/clients: both are handled the same way
export type TypePersonnes = 'medecins' | 'clients';

type Vide = Record<string, never>;
type Methode = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE';

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class RdvMedecinsApi {
  private readonly http = inject(HttpClient);

   // the request itself; public: true for routes that handle
   // the 401 error themselves (public routes, GET /api/auth/moi)
  private requete<T>(methode: Methode, url: string, corps?: unknown, publique = false, params?: HttpParams): Promise<T> {
    return firstValueFrom(
      this.http.request<T>(methode, `/api${url}`, {
        body: corps,
        params,
        context: new HttpContext().set(IGNORER_401, publique),
      }),
    );
  }

   // ------------------------------------------------ login (public routes)
  captcha(): Promise<Captcha> {
    return this.requete<Captcha>('GET', '/captcha', undefined, true);
  }
  moi(): Promise<Utilisateur> {
    return this.requete<Utilisateur>('GET', '/auth/moi', undefined, true);
  }
  connecter(login: string, password: string, captchaId: string, captcha: string): Promise<Utilisateur> {
    return this.requete<Utilisateur>('POST', '/auth/login', { login, password, captchaId, captcha }, true);
  }
  deconnecter(): Promise<Vide> {
    return this.requete<Vide>('POST', '/auth/logout', {}, true);
  }

   // ------------------------------------------------ account creation (public)
  accesInscription(captchaId: string, captcha: string): Promise<Vide> {
    return this.requete<Vide>('POST', '/inscription/acces', { captchaId, captcha }, true);
  }
  etatAccesInscription(): Promise<{ valide: boolean }> {
    return this.requete<{ valide: boolean }>('GET', '/inscription/acces', undefined, true);
  }
  inscrire(donnees: Inscription): Promise<{ login: string }> {
    return this.requete<{ login: string }>('POST', '/inscription', donnees, true);
  }

   // ------------------------------------------------ calendar and appointments
   // idMedecin null: for a logged-in doctor, SON calendar
  agenda(idMedecin: number | null, jour: string): Promise<Agenda> {
    let params = new HttpParams().set('jour', jour);
    if (idMedecin !== null) {
      params = params.set('idMedecin', idMedecin);
    }
    return this.requete<Agenda>('GET', '/agenda', undefined, false, params);
  }
  reserver(jour: string, idCreneau: number, idClient: number | null): Promise<{ id: number }> {
    return this.requete<{ id: number }>('POST', '/rendez-vous', { jour, idCreneau, idClient: idClient ?? undefined });
  }
  annulerRv(idRv: number): Promise<Vide> {
    return this.requete<Vide>('DELETE', `/rendez-vous/${idRv}`);
  }

   // ------------------------------------------------ doctors and clients
  lister(type: TypePersonnes): Promise<Personne[]> {
    return this.requete<Personne[]>('GET', `/${type}`);
  }
  lire(type: TypePersonnes, id: number): Promise<Personne> {
    return this.requete<Personne>('GET', `/${type}/${id}`);
  }
  ajouter(type: TypePersonnes, donnees: DonneesPersonne): Promise<Personne> {
    return this.requete<Personne>('POST', `/${type}`, donnees);
  }
  modifier(type: TypePersonnes, id: number, donnees: DonneesPersonne): Promise<Personne> {
    return this.requete<Personne>('PUT', `/${type}/${id}`, donnees);
  }
  supprimer(type: TypePersonnes, id: number): Promise<Vide> {
    return this.requete<Vide>('DELETE', `/${type}/${id}`);
  }

   // ------------------------------------------------ the patient portal
  monEspace(): Promise<MonEspace> {
    return this.requete<MonEspace>('GET', '/mon-espace');
  }
  monCompte(): Promise<MonCompte> {
    return this.requete<MonCompte>('GET', '/mon-compte');
  }
  modifierMonCompte(donnees: ModificationMonCompte): Promise<Utilisateur> {
    return this.requete<Utilisateur>('PUT', '/mon-compte', donnees);
  }
  supprimerMonCompte(motDePasseActuel: string): Promise<Vide> {
    return this.requete<Vide>('DELETE', '/mon-compte', { motDePasseActuel });
  }
}

The API access layer: one method per route.

  • Lines 40–48: A single method handles all requests. [http.request] accepts the method HTTP as a parameter; [firstValueFrom] turns it into a promise;
  • line 45: the request carries the context token [IGNORER_401]: true for routes that handle the 401 themselves. An incorrect password returns a 401: this is not an expired session! Similarly, [GET /api/auth/moi] returns a 401 when no one is logged in, which is normal;
  • lines 77–83: [HttpParams] generates the URL parameters (?day=...&idMedecin=...). An object [HttpParams] does not change: [set] returns a new object;
  • line 85: [idClient ?? undefined]: if a [idClient] is missing, it is not sent at all;
  • Lines 92–106: Doctors and clients are handled the same way: the type (['medecins'] or ['clients']) is part of the address;
  • line 119: a DELETE with a body containing the current password, required to delete the account.

// =========================================================================
// i18n/i18n.ts - French and English (ngx-translate, see Example 21)
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The dictionaries fr.json and en.json are those from the course NestJS
// (i18n/*.json), supplemented with a few client-specific keys
// (ERRORS.SERVER_UNREACHABLE...). The JSON server returns only CLÉS
// ('ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN'): these are the same as those in the dictionaries.
//
// The selected language is stored in localStorage (a preference, not
// sensitive data); otherwise, the browser’s language is used.
// =========================================================================

import { Provider } from '@angular/core';
import { provideTranslateLoader, provideTranslateService, TranslateLoader, TranslationObject } from '@ngx-translate/core';
import { Observable, of } from 'rxjs';
import fr from './fr.json';
import en from './en.json';

export type Langue = 'fr' | 'en';
export const LANGUES: Langue[] = ['fr', 'en'];
export const CLE_STOCKAGE = 'rdvmedecins.langue';

// The dictionaries are part of the application code: no request
class DictionnairesLoader implements TranslateLoader {
  getTranslation(langue: string): Observable<TranslationObject> {
    return of(langue === 'en' ? en : fr);
  }
}

export function langueDeDepart(): Langue {
  try {
    const memorisee = localStorage.getItem(CLE_STOCKAGE);
    if (memorisee === 'fr' || memorisee === 'en') {
      return memorisee;
    }
  } catch {
     // localStorage unavailable (strict private browsing...): oh well
  }
  return navigator.language.toLowerCase().startsWith('en') ? 'en' : 'fr';
}

export function provideI18n(): Provider[] {
  return provideTranslateService({
    loader: provideTranslateLoader(DictionnairesLoader),
    fallbackLang: 'fr',
    lang: langueDeDepart(),
  });
}

The configuration of [ngx-translate] from Example 21:

  • Lines 30–40: The source language is the one the user last selected; otherwise, it is the browser's language. Access to [localStorage] may fail (in certain private browsing modes), so we skip it in that case.

// =========================================================================
// i18n/langue.service.ts - the current language, and how to change it
// =========================================================================

import { inject, Injectable } from '@angular/core';
import { TranslateService } from '@ngx-translate/core';
import { CLE_STOCKAGE, Langue } from './i18n';

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class LangueService {
  private readonly translate = inject(TranslateService);
   // a flag: 'fr' or 'en'
  readonly langue = this.translate.currentLang;

  constructor() {
    document.documentElement.lang = this.translate.getCurrentLang() ?? 'fr';
  }

   // change languages: the entire app is immediately re-translated
  changer(langue: Langue): void {
    this.translate.use(langue);
    document.documentElement.lang = langue;
    try {
      localStorage.setItem(CLE_STOCKAGE, langue);
    } catch {
       // irrelevant
    }
  }
}
  • line 13: the current language, a flag;
  • lines 20–28: change language: the page is re-translated (line 21), the page’s [lang] attribute is updated (line 22), and the selection is saved (line 24).

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// i18n/titre.strategy.ts - the tab title, translated
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Each route declares a title (title: 'AGENDA.PAGE_TITLE', see
// app.routes.ts). By default, Angular displays it as TEL QUEL in the tab. A
// TitleStrategy overrides this behavior: updateTitle() is called after
// each navigation; buildTitle() returns the title of the displayed route
// (in this case, a key), which is translated. And when the language changes, it is retranslated
// the most recent title.
// The class is declared in app.config.ts:
//      { provide: TitleStrategy, useClass: TitreTraduit }
// =========================================================================

import { inject, Injectable } from '@angular/core';
import { Title } from '@angular/platform-browser';
import { RouterStateSnapshot, TitleStrategy } from '@angular/router';
import { TranslateService } from '@ngx-translate/core';

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class TitreTraduit extends TitleStrategy {
  private readonly title = inject(Title);
  private readonly translate = inject(TranslateService);
  private cle: string | undefined;

  constructor() {
    super();
    this.translate.onLangChange.subscribe(() => this.appliquer());
  }

  override updateTitle(snapshot: RouterStateSnapshot): void {
    this.cle = this.buildTitle(snapshot);
    this.appliquer();
  }

  private appliquer(): void {
    const application = this.translate.instant('APP.TITLE');
    this.title.setTitle(this.cle ? `${this.translate.instant(this.cle)} - ${application}` : application);
  }
}

Each route declares a title, which in this case is a translation key ('AGENDA.PAGE_TITLE'). By default, [Angular] would write it as-is in the tab. This class replaces the router’s [TitleStrategy] service (app.config.ts, line 23):

  • line 20: it inherits the [TitleStrategy] class from [Angular];
  • lines 30–33: [updateTitle] is called by the router after each navigation; [buildTitle], which is inherited, provides the title declared by the displayed route;
  • lines 35–38: the translated title, followed by the application name: “Calendar - RdvMedecins”;
  • line 27: when the language changes, the last title is retranslated.

docs.title: 10.4.5.1. src/app/services/session.service.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// services/session.service.ts - Is QUI logged in?
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The logged-in user (or null), and what we can infer from that (is it ADMIN?
// patient?), in a root service with signals (see Example 20).
//
// The JWT token itself is not present here: it is stored in a httpOnly cookie that
// only the browser handles. The service only stores the DESCRIPTION of
// the user, returned by the server ({ login, name, role }).
//
// Upon startup (and after a F5), the service is empty: verifier() requests
// the server, just once, to find out who is logged in (GET /api/auth/moi).
// =========================================================================

import { computed, inject, Injectable, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { RdvMedecinsApi } from '../api/rdvmedecins.api';
import { Role, Utilisateur } from '../api/types';

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class SessionService {
  private readonly api = inject(RdvMedecinsApi);
  private readonly _utilisateur = signal<Utilisateur | null>(null);
   // Has the question “Who is logged in?” already been asked of the server?
  private verification: Promise<void> | null = null;

  readonly utilisateur = this._utilisateur.asReadonly();
  readonly connecte = computed(() => this._utilisateur() !== null);
  readonly role = computed<Role | null>(() => this._utilisateur()?.role ?? null);
  readonly estAdmin = computed(() => this.role() === 'ADMIN');
  readonly estPatient = computed(() => this.role() === 'USER');
   // ADMIN and DOCTOR: schedule and cancel appointments for any patient
  readonly estGestionnaire = computed(() => this.role() === 'ADMIN' || this.role() === 'DOCTOR');

   // The home page for each role, immediately after logging in
  readonly pageAccueil = computed(() => (this.estPatient() ? '/mon-espace' : '/agenda'));

   // called by the router guard before CHAQUE navigation; does not query
   // the server only the first time (the token is retained and reused)
  verifier(): Promise<void> {
    this.verification ??= this.api
      .moi()
      .then((u) => this._utilisateur.set(u))
      .catch(() => this._utilisateur.set(null)); // 401: No such user; or server unreachable
    return this.verification;
  }

  async connecter(login: string, password: string, captchaId: string, captcha: string): Promise<void> {
    this._utilisateur.set(await this.api.connecter(login, password, captchaId, captcha));
  }

   // The user has changed their name or login (PUT /api/my-account)
  mettreAJour(u: Utilisateur): void {
    this._utilisateur.set(u);
  }

  async deconnecter(): Promise<void> {
    try {
      await this.api.deconnecter();
    } finally {
      this.oublier();
    }
  }

   // Without making a request to the server: session expired, account deleted
  oublier(): void {
    this._utilisateur.set(null);
  }
}

The logged-in user, in a signal service (example 20):

  • line 22: the state: the user, or [null]. The token itself is not here: it is in a cookie that only the browser handles;
  • lines 26–32: what the components read: the user, and what is inferred from that (is the user logged in? ADMIN? a patient?);
  • line 35: the home page for each role;
  • lines 39–45: upon startup (and after a F5), the service does not know who is logged in: it asks the server. [verifier] is called by the router guard before CHAQUE navigation, but only queries the server the first time: the promise is kept (line 40, [??=]: “if it does not yet exist”) and is returned with each subsequent call. If two navigations follow each other closely, they expect the same response;
  • line 43: 401 (no one) or server unreachable: no user;
  • lines 56–62: logout; [finally]: the user is forgotten even if the server does not respond;
  • lines 65–67: forget the user without sending a request to the server: this is what the interceptor does on a 401.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// services/messages.service.ts - messages displayed to the user
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Same layout as the HTML application:
//    - a SUCCÈS is displayed as HAUT on the page (green banner);
//    - a ERREUR appears as BAS, on a light pink background (the “sticky” area).
// A message is a translation CLÉ (plus its settings): it is therefore re-translated
// on its own if the user changes the language.
//
// "Flash" messages: an action that ends with a page change
// page (booking, adding a doctor, etc.) places its message using flash();
// it will be displayed on the SUIVANTE page, then disappear upon subsequent navigation
// the user navigates to the next page. The service knows this because it listens for router events
// (end of each navigation). On the server side, this was the role of the
// short-lived cookie “rdvmedecins_flash.”
// =========================================================================

import { Injectable, inject, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { NavigationEnd, Router } from '@angular/router';
import { ErreurApi } from '../api/erreur-api';

export interface Message {
  cle: string;
  params?: Record<string, string>;
}

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class MessagesService {
  readonly succes = signal<Message | null>(null);
  readonly erreur = signal<Message | null>(null);
   // the messages to display on the next page
  private enAttente: { succes: Message | null; erreur: Message | null } | null = null;

  constructor() {
     // a new page (including when only the query changes, /agenda?...) is loaded:
     // the messages from the previous page disappear, and the flash messages
     // appear. A root service lives as long as the application:
     // no need to unsubscribe.
    inject(Router).events.subscribe((e) => {
      if (e instanceof NavigationEnd) {
        this.nouvellePage();
      }
    });
  }

  afficherSucces(cle: string, params?: Record<string, string>): void {
    this.succes.set({ cle, params });
    this.erreur.set(null);
  }

  afficherErreur(cle: string, params?: Record<string, string>): void {
    this.erreur.set({ cle, params });
    this.succes.set(null);
  }

   // a ErreurApi -> the page message; any other error is a
   // client-side issue, which should be logged (browser console)
  afficherErreurApi(e: unknown): void {
    if (!(e instanceof ErreurApi)) {
      throw e;
    }
    this.afficherErreur(e.cle, e.params);
  }

  effacer(): void {
    this.succes.set(null);
    this.erreur.set(null);
  }

   // for the page SUIVANTE
  flash(type: 'succes' | 'erreur', cle: string, params?: Record<string, string>): void {
    this.enAttente ??= { succes: null, erreur: null };
    this.enAttente[type] = { cle, params };
  }

  private nouvellePage(): void {
    this.succes.set(this.enAttente?.succes ?? null);
    this.erreur.set(this.enAttente?.erreur ?? null);
    this.enAttente = null;
  }
}

Messages displayed to the user, as in the HTML application: a success message at the top of the page, an error message at the bottom. A message is a translation key: it translates itself automatically if the user changes languages.

  • Lines 29–30: the two messages on the current page;
  • lines 58–63: a [ErreurApi] becomes the page’s error message; any other error is a client-side issue, which is allowed to be reported;
  • lines 71–74: a flash message for the next page. An action that ends with a page change (a doctor added, return to the list) thus displays its message;
  • lines 39–43: the service listens for router events (example 17). At the end of each navigation session (lines 76–80), the messages from the previous page disappear and the flash messages appear. On the server side, this was the role of a short-lived cookie.

// =========================================================================
// services/confirmation.service.ts - “Are you sure?”
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Taken from Example 16: confirm(key) opens the confirmation window
// (components/fenetre-confirmation.ts, placed once in App) and returns
// a promise resolved to true (Yes) or false (No). The message is a CLÉ
// translation: the window translates it into the current language.
//
//      if (await this.confirmation.confirmer('AGENDA.CANCEL_CONFIRM')) { ... }
// =========================================================================

import { inject, Injectable, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { MessagesService } from './messages.service';

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class ConfirmationService {
  private readonly messages = inject(MessagesService);
  private readonly _cleMessage = signal<string | null>(null); // null: window closed
  readonly cleMessage = this._cleMessage.asReadonly();
  private repondre: ((oui: boolean) => void) | null = null;

  confirmer(cle: string): Promise<boolean> {
    this.repondre?.(false); // Is there still an open question? It is "no"
     // a new question: messages from the previous action are out of date
    this.messages.effacer();
    this._cleMessage.set(cle);
    return new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => {
      this.repondre = resolve;
    });
  }

  reponse(oui: boolean): void {
    this._cleMessage.set(null);
    const r = this.repondre;
    this.repondre = null;
    r?.(oui);
  }
}

The service from Example 16. The message is now a translation key (line 18), and a new query clears the messages from the previous action (line 25).

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// services/envoi-formulaire.ts - send a form to the server
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// All forms in the application follow the same pattern as
// Example 25: No rules are checked in the browser (they
// are handled in UN one place only—the server), and in case of rejection:
//    - the error for each field (ErreurApi.champs) is attached to the corresponding field in the
//      form’s error messages, which displays it with a red border;
//    - the general message (ErreurApi.cle) appears at the bottom of the page.
// This class groups these actions. A page creates one per form:
//
//      protected readonly submission = new EnvoiFormulaire(this.f);
//      if (await this.envoi.envoyer(() => this.api.inscrire(this.modele()))) { ... }
//
// It is used in an injection context (initialization of a field
// of the component class): there, it retrieves the message service.
// =========================================================================

import { inject, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { FieldTree, isFieldTree, submit, ValidationError } from '@angular/forms/signals';
import { ErreurApi } from '../api/erreur-api';
import { MessagesService } from './messages.service';

export class EnvoiFormulaire<T> {
  private readonly messages = inject(MessagesService);
   // the error message parameters ({min}...), returned by the server
  readonly params = signal<Record<string, string>>({});

  constructor(private readonly formulaire: FieldTree<T>) {}

   // executes the send; returns true if successful. In case of an error, the
   // errors are displayed and false is returned.
   // ignorerValidateurs: Send even if the form schema rules
   // (if any) are not met
  async envoyer(action: () => Promise<unknown>, ignorerValidateurs = false): Promise<boolean> {
    this.params.set({});
    let reussi = false;
    await submit(this.formulaire, {
      ignoreValidators: ignorerValidateurs ? 'all' : 'pending',
      action: async () => {
        try {
          await action();
          reussi = true;
          return null; // no errors
        } catch (e) {
          this.messages.afficherErreurApi(e); // (re-sends any error that is not a ErreurApi)
          const erreur = e as ErreurApi;
          this.params.set(erreur.params);
          return this.erreursDesChamps(erreur);
        }
      },
    });
    return reussi;
  }

   // { name: 'ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED' } -> an error associated with the field f.nom
  private erreursDesChamps(e: ErreurApi): ValidationError.WithOptionalFieldTree[] {
    const champs = this.formulaire as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
    return Object.entries(e.champs)
      .filter(([nom]) => isFieldTree(champs[nom]))
      .map(([nom, cle]) => ({ kind: 'serveur', message: cle, fieldTree: champs[nom] as FieldTree<unknown> }));
  }
}

All forms in the application follow the pattern shown in Example 25: the rules are validated by the server, and if a form is rejected, the error for each field is displayed below that field, with a general error message at the bottom of the page. This class groups these actions together so they don’t have to be repeated on every page:

  • line 24: a generic class: [T] is the form template type;

// =========================================================================
// pipes/formatage.ts - displaying people, hours, and days
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The server sends data BRUTES (start_hour: 8, start_minute: 0; day:
// "2026-10-05"); the formatting, which depends on the language, is the responsibility
// the client. Functions used by the code and pipes (file
// formatage.pipes.ts), used by the templates.
// =========================================================================

import { Creneau, Identite } from '../api/types';

// "Ms. Alice DURAND"
export function libelle(p: Identite): string {
  return `${p.titre} ${p.prenom} ${p.nom}`;
}

// "8:05" rather than "8:5"
export function heure(h: number, m: number): string {
  return `${h}:${String(m).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

// "8:00 - 8:20"
export function horaire(c: Creneau): string {
  return `${heure(c.hdebut, c.mdebut)} - ${heure(c.hfin, c.mfin)}`;
}

// today's date, in "yyyy-MM-dd" format (the same as <input type="date"> and API)
export function aujourdhui(): string {
  const d = new Date();
  return `${d.getFullYear()}-${String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

// true if [jour] is a valid date in the yyyy-MM-dd format
export function estUneDateValide(jour: unknown): jour is string {
  if (typeof jour !== 'string' || !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(jour)) {
    return false;
  }
  const date = new Date(`${jour}T00:00:00Z`);
  return !isNaN(date.getTime()) && date.toISOString().slice(0, 10) === jour;
}

// "Monday, October 5, 2026" / "Monday 5 October 2026"
export function jourLong(jour: string, langue: string | null): string {
  return new Intl.DateTimeFormat(langue === 'en' ? 'en-GB' : 'fr-FR', {
    dateStyle: 'full',
    timeZone: 'UTC', // "2026-10-05T00:00:00Z" must remain 5, regardless of the time zone
  }).format(new Date(`${jour}T00:00:00Z`));
}

The server sends raw data ([hdebut: 8, mdebut: 0]; [jour: "2026-10-05"]); formatting, which depends on the language, is the client’s responsibility:

  • lines 34–40: Is this a valid date? [2026-02-30] has the correct format, but does not exist: [new Date] would convert it to March 2. We therefore verify that it reads identically. [jour is string]: if the function returns true, [TypeScript] knows that [jour] is a string;
  • lines 43–48: [Intl.DateTimeFormat], provided by the browser, writes the date in the requested language. The time zone UTC prevents a browser located west of Greenwich from displaying the previous day.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// pipes/formatage.pipes.ts - the functions of formatage.ts, separated by pipes
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
//      {{ doctor | title }}          "Ms. Marie PELISSIER"
//      {{ time slot | sched         ule }} "8:00 - 8:20"
//      {{ day | jourLong: language( ) }} "Monday, October 5, 2026"
// jourLong receives the language as a parameter: a pure pipe is only recalculated
// If any of its arguments change, the language-switching function recalculates it.
// =========================================================================

import { Pipe, PipeTransform } from '@angular/core';
import { Creneau, Identite } from '../api/types';
import { horaire, jourLong, libelle } from './formatage';

@Pipe({ name: 'libelle' })
export class LibellePipe implements PipeTransform {
  transform(p: Identite): string {
    return libelle(p);
  }
}

@Pipe({ name: 'horaire' })
export class HorairePipe implements PipeTransform {
  transform(c: Creneau): string {
    return horaire(c);
  }
}

@Pipe({ name: 'jourLong' })
export class JourLongPipe implements PipeTransform {
  transform(jour: string, langue: string | null): string {
    return jourLong(jour, langue);
  }
}

The same functions, as pipes, for templates. [jourLong] receives the language as a parameter: a pure pipe (e.g., 09) is recalculated only if one of its arguments changes; changing the language therefore triggers a recalculation.

// =========================================================================
// app.routes.ts - the application's pages and their access permissions
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The MÊMES URLs that the HTML application (/login, /agenda, /doctors,
// /my-space...), but these are now routes in CLIENT. The
// browser only sends a request to the server for the very first
// page; afterward, the router changes the address and the displayed component.
//
// The flip side of the coin: if the user reloads /agenda (F5), the
// browser does indeed request /agenda from the server, which must then
// return index.html (ng-serve does this in development; in production,
// see web/client-spa.ts on the JSON server).
//
// All pages are the ENFANTS (children) of a route without a component,
// which carries the guard gardeSession (canActivateChild): it thus applies
// to each of them. Each route declares:
//    - title: translation key for the tab title (see i18n/titre.strategy.ts);
//    - dat a: public (accessible without logging in), roles (authorized roles
//              authorized), type (“doctors” or “clients”), code (403, 404).
// Thanks to withComponentInputBinding (app.config.ts), the parameters
// the address (:id, ?day=...) and ET the data (type, code) are passed to the
// ENTRÉES page components.
// =========================================================================

import { Routes } from '@angular/router';
import { TypePersonnes } from './api/rdvmedecins.api';
import { Role } from './api/types';
import { gardeInscription, gardeSession, idNumerique } from './gardes';
import { ConnexionPage } from './pages/connexion/connexion';
import { AgendaPage } from './pages/agenda/agenda';

// the management routes for doctors ET and clients (ADMIN), on the same
// template; pages are loaded on demand (loadComponent)
function routesPersonnes(type: TypePersonnes, titre: string, titreAjout: string, titreModif: string): Routes {
  const data = { roles: ['ADMIN'] as Role[], type };
  return [
    { path: type, loadComponent: () => import('./pages/personnes/personnes'), title: titre, data },
    { path: `${type}/ajouter`, loadComponent: () => import('./pages/personne-formulaire/personne-formulaire'), title: titreAjout, data },
    {
      path: `${type}/:id/modifier`,
      canMatch: [idNumerique],
      loadComponent: () => import('./pages/personne-formulaire/personne-formulaire'),
      title: titreModif,
      data,
    },
  ];
}

export const routes: Routes = [
  {
    path: '',
    canActivateChild: [gardeSession],
    children: [
       // "/": to /login, which in turn redirects to the role’s home page if the user is logged in
      { path: '', pathMatch: 'full', redirectTo: 'login' },
      { path: 'login', component: ConnexionPage, title: 'LOGIN.TITLE', data: { public: true } },
      { path: 'agenda', component: AgendaPage, title: 'AGENDA.PAGE_TITLE' },
      ...routesPersonnes('medecins', 'MEDECINS.TITLE', 'MEDECINS.ADD', 'MEDECINS.EDIT'),
      ...routesPersonnes('clients', 'CLIENTS.TITLE', 'CLIENTS.ADD', 'CLIENTS.EDIT'),
      {
        path: 'inscription',
        loadComponent: () => import('./pages/inscription/inscription'),
        title: 'INSCRIPTION.TITLE',
        data: { public: true },
        canActivate: [gardeInscription],
      },
      {
        path: 'mon-espace',
        loadComponent: () => import('./pages/espace-patient/espace-patient'),
        title: 'ESPACE.TITLE',
        data: { roles: ['USER'] },
      },
      {
        path: 'mon-compte',
        loadComponent: () => import('./pages/mon-compte/mon-compte'),
        title: 'MON_COMPTE.TITLE',
        data: { roles: ['USER'] },
      },
      { path: 'interdit', loadComponent: () => import('./pages/erreur/erreur'), title: 'ERROR_PAGE.TITLE', data: { code: 403 } },
      {
        path: '**',
        loadComponent: () => import('./pages/erreur/erreur'),
        title: 'ERROR_PAGE.TITLE',
        data: { code: 404, public: true },
      },
    ],
  },
];

The same URLs as the HTML application (/login, /agenda, /doctors, /my-space...), but these are now client routes:

  • lines 50–53: all pages are children ([children]) of a route without a component, which carries the guard [gardeSession]: [canActivateChild] applies it to each of them without having to repeat it;
  • line 55: the address / leads to the login page, which in turn redirects to the role’s home page if the user is logged in;
  • lines 56–57: the two most-visited pages are part of the main file; the others are loaded on demand ([loadComponent]);
  • [title]: the translation key for the tab title;
  • [data]: [public] (accessible without being logged in), [roles] (authorized roles; absent: all logged-in roles), [type] (['medecins'] or ['clients']), [code] (403, 404). Thanks to [withComponentInputBinding], the route data is also passed into the page component’s inputs, such as the address parameters;
  • lines 34–47: The three routes for the doctor management system and those for the client management system are generated by the same function: both systems use the same pages, with a different [type];
  • line 41: [canMatch]: a guard that determines whether the route matches the address. If it fails, the router tries the following routes: /doctors/abc/edit thus leads to a 404 page;
  • line 65: a guard specific to the account creation page;
  • line 79: the 403 page, to which the guard redirects;
  • lines 80–85: any other address: the 404 page.

docs.title: 10.4.7.2. src/app/gardes.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// gardes.ts - the router's guards
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// gardeSession: the guard for TOUTES pages (see app.routes.ts). Before
// each time you browse:
//    1. The first time (startup, F5), it asks the server who is
//       connected (SessionService.verifier);
//    2. It checks the permissions described in the route data:
//         - public: accessible without being logged in;
//         -  roles: authorized roles (none = all logged-in roles).
//
// RAPPEL: These checks are merely a CONFORT (do not display a page
// is unnecessary). Data protection is handled by the server, which
// verifies the token and role in the CHAQUE request.
//
// ATTENTION: inject() is only allowed by a guard, before any
// await (afterward, the "injection context" is lost).
// =========================================================================

import { inject } from '@angular/core';
import { CanActivateChildFn, CanActivateFn, CanMatchFn, Router } from '@angular/router';
import { Role } from './api/types';
import { RdvMedecinsApi } from './api/rdvmedecins.api';
import { SessionService } from './services/session.service';
import { MessagesService } from './services/messages.service';

export const gardeSession: CanActivateChildFn = async (route, etat) => {
  const session = inject(SessionService);
  const router = inject(Router);
  await session.verifier();

  if (route.data['public']) {
     // Already logged in: the login page is no longer relevant
    if (route.routeConfig?.path === 'login' && session.connecte()) {
      return router.parseUrl(session.pageAccueil());
    }
    return true;
  }
  if (!session.connecte()) {
     // we keep the requested page to return to it after logging in
    return router.createUrlTree(['/login'], { queryParams: { redirect: etat.url } });
  }
  const roles = route.data['roles'] as Role[] | undefined;
  if (roles && !roles.includes(session.role()!)) {
    return router.createUrlTree(['/interdit']);
  }
  return true;
};

// a guard PROPRE on the /registration route: no pass (captcha
// resolved on the login page), return to the login page
export const gardeInscription: CanActivateFn = async () => {
  const api = inject(RdvMedecinsApi);
  const messages = inject(MessagesService);
  const router = inject(Router);
  const { valide } = await api.etatAccesInscription().catch(() => ({ valide: false }));
  if (!valide) {
    messages.flash('erreur', 'ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT');
    return router.createUrlTree(['/login']);
  }
  return true;
};

// /doctors/3/edit: the route only works if the second segment of
// the address is a number (/doctors/abc/edit leads to a 404 page)
export const idNumerique: CanMatchFn = (_route, segments) => /^\d+$/.test(segments[1]?.path ?? '');
  • Line 27: A guard can be [async]: The router is waiting for its response;
  • Lines 28–30: ATTENTION: [inject] is only allowed at the beginning of the guard, before any [await]; after that, the injection context is lost;
  • line 30: the first time, the server is asked who is logged in;
  • lines 32–38: a public page; but the login page no longer makes sense for a logged-in user (line 34). [parseUrl] converts an address to [UrlTree], the value that triggers a redirect;
  • lines 39–42: not logged in: to the login page, while retaining the requested page;
  • lines 43–46: an invalid role: redirects to the 403 page;
  • lines 52–62: creating an account requires a “pass,” obtained by solving the CAPTCHA on the login page. Without it, the user is returned to the login page with a message;
  • line 66: the guard [canMatch] receives the address segments: [['medecins', '3', 'modifier']].

These guards are merely a convenience: data protection is ensured by the server, which re-verifies the token and role with every request.

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// components/confirmation-window/fenetre-confirmation.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The “Are you sure?” window from Example 16, completed for keyboard use
// as public/js/app.js from the HTML application:
//    - Upon opening, the focus goes to "No, go back": an accidental press of
//      Enter does not delete anything;
//    - Esc closes the window (= No);
//    - Tab and Shift+Tab keep the focus on DANS the window (otherwise the focus would move to
//      the grayed-out page behind it);
//    - Upon closing, the focus returns to the element that had it (the
//      "Delete" button that was clicked, for example).
// "No, go back" rather than "Cancel": the question is sometimes “Cancel this
// appointment?", and a "Cancel" button there would be ambiguous.
// =========================================================================

import { Component, effect, ElementRef, inject, untracked, viewChild } from '@angular/core';
import { TranslatePipe } from '@ngx-translate/core';
import { ConfirmationService } from '../../services/confirmation.service';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-fenetre-confirmation',
  imports: [TranslatePipe],
  templateUrl: './fenetre-confirmation.html',
})
export class FenetreConfirmation {
  protected readonly confirmation = inject(ConfirmationService);
  private readonly fenetre = viewChild<ElementRef<HTMLElement>>('fenetre');
  private readonly boutonNon = viewChild<ElementRef<HTMLButtonElement>>('boutonNon');
  private focusPrecedent: HTMLElement | null = null;

  constructor() {
     // the window opens (the “No” button appears) or closes
    effect(() => {
      const bouton = this.boutonNon();
      untracked(() => {
        if (bouton) {
          this.focusPrecedent = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;
          bouton.nativeElement.focus();
        } else {
          this.focusPrecedent?.focus();
          this.focusPrecedent = null;
        }
      });
    });
  }

  protected clavier(e: KeyboardEvent): void {
    const fenetre = this.fenetre()?.nativeElement;
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      this.confirmation.reponse(false);
    } else if (e.key === 'Tab' && fenetre) {
      const boutons = [...fenetre.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>('button')];
      const premier = boutons[0];
      const dernier = boutons[boutons.length - 1];
      if (e.shiftKey && document.activeElement === premier) {
        e.preventDefault();
        dernier?.focus();
      } else if (!e.shiftKey && document.activeElement === dernier) {
        e.preventDefault();
        premier?.focus();
      }
    }
  }

   // clicking on the grayed-out background (not inside the window itself) = No
  protected clicFond(e: MouseEvent): void {
    if (e.target === e.currentTarget) {
      this.confirmation.reponse(false);
    }
  }
}

The window from Example 16, with keyboard support added:

  • lines 34–45: an effect that follows the appearance and disappearance of the “No” button. Upon opening, the element that had focus is retained, and focus is given to the “No” button; upon closing, focus returns to the retained element (the “Delete” button that was clicked, for example). [untracked]: the signals read in this function do not become dependencies of the effect;
  • lines 48–64: the keyboard. Esc responds with “no”; Tab and Shift+Tab remain within the window: from the last button, you return to the first, and vice versa. Otherwise, focus would move to the grayed-out page behind it;
  • lines 67–71: a click on the grayed-out background responds with “no.”

  <div (keydown)="clavier($event)">
    <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
    <div #window class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"
         aria-labelledby="confirmation-titre" aria-describedby="confirmation-message" (click)="clicFond($event)">
      <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
        <div class="modal-content">
          <div class="modal-header">
            <h5 id="confirmation-titre" class="modal-title">{{ 'CONFIRMATION.TITLE' | translate }}</h5>
            <button type="button" class="btn-close" [attr.aria-label]="'BOOKING_DIALOG.CLOSE_ARIA' | translate"
                    (click)="confirmation.reponse(false)"></button>
          </div>
          <div class="modal-body">
            <p id="confirmation-message" class="mb-0">{{ cle | translate }}</p>
          </div>
          <div class="modal-footer">
            <button #boutonNon type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" (click)="confirmation.reponse(false)">
              {{ 'CONFIRMATION.NO' | translate }}
            </button>
            <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" (click)="confirmation.reponse(true)">{{ 'CONFIRMATION.YES' | translate }}</button>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>

}

// =========================================================================
// components/champ-saisie.ts - a complete form field
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Label + field + tooltip OU error message. All
// forms in the application use it, including a form with indicators:
//
//    <app-input-field [formField]="f.nom" idChamp="name" label="PERSONNES.LASTNAME_LABEL" [longueurMax]="20" />
//
// This is a CONTRÔLE DE FORMULAIRE "house": by implementing the interface
// FormValueControl, it accepts [formField] as a regular <input>.
// The contract is simple:
//    - value (a model()): the value of the field, read and written by the
//      form;
//    - errors (an optional contract entry): if the component
//      declares it, the [formField] directive stores the field’s errors there—
//      here, those returned by SERVEUR (see pages/personne-formulaire.ts).
// The label, help text, and error messages are translations from CLÉS.
// =========================================================================

import { booleanAttribute, Component, computed, input, model } from '@angular/core';
import { FormValueControl, ValidationError } from '@angular/forms/signals';
import { TranslatePipe } from '@ngx-translate/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-champ-saisie',
  imports: [TranslatePipe],
   // A component is displayed "inline" by default: we turn it into a block,
   // so that the classes set by the parent (mb-3, col-sm-6) apply
  styles: `
    :host {
      display: block;
    }
  `,
  template: `
    <label class="form-label" [for]="idChamp()">{{ libelle() | translate }}</label>
    <input class="form-control" [id]="idChamp()" [type]="type()" [value]="value()" (input)="saisir($event)"
           [class.is-invalid]="erreur()" [attr.maxlength]="longueurMax() ?? null" [autocomplete]="autocomplete()"
           [required]="requis()" [attr.aria-invalid]="erreur() ? 'true' : null" [attr.aria-describedby]="idChamp() + '-message'">
    @if (erreur(); as e) {
      <div class="invalid-feedback" [id]="idChamp() + '-message'">{{ e | translate: params() }}</div>
    } @else if (aide(); as a) {
      <div class="form-text" [id]="idChamp() + '-message'">{{ a | translate: params() }}</div>
    }
  `,
})
export class ChampSaisie implements FormValueControl<string> {
   // the contract FormValueControl
  readonly value = model('');
  readonly errors = input<readonly ValidationError.WithOptionalFieldTree[]>([]);

   // our own entries
   // the ID of the <input> (not "id": an "id" attribute would remain AUSSI set on
   // <app-input-field>, and the page would have two elements with the same id)
  readonly idChamp = input.required<string>();
  readonly libelle = input.required<string>(); // translation key
  readonly type = input<'text' | 'password'>('text');
  readonly aide = input<string>(); // help message key
  readonly params = input<Record<string, string>>({}); // message parameters ({min}...)
  readonly longueurMax = input<number>();
  readonly autocomplete = input('off');
  readonly requis = input(false, { transform: booleanAttribute });

   // the first error for the field (its translation key), if there is one
  protected readonly erreur = computed(() => this.errors()[0]?.message);

  protected saisir(evenement: Event): void {
    this.value.set((evenement.target as HTMLInputElement).value);
  }
}

A complete form field: label, field, tooltip, or error message. All forms in the application use it. It is a custom form control: by adhering to the [FormValueControl] contract, it accepts the [[formField]] directive as a regular [<input>]:

  • line 46: the class implements the [FormValueControl<string>] interface: the compiler verifies that it complies with the contract;
  • line 48: [value], a [model()] (Example 11): the value of the field that the [[formField]] directive reads and ET writes;
  • line 49: [errors], an optional entry in the contract: if the component declares it, the directive stores the field’s errors there;
  • lines 54–61: component-specific entries. The identifier for the element [<input>] is named [idChamp], not [id]: an attribute [id] set on [<app-champ-saisie>] would also remain set on this element, and the page would have two elements with the same identifier;
  • line 61: [booleanAttribute] changes the presence of the attribute ([requis], with no value) to [true];
  • line 64: the first error in the field: its translation key;
  • Lines 36–38: The [<input>] element displays the value and returns it with each keystroke (lines 66–68). [aria-invalid] and [aria-describedby] link the field to its message for screen readers;
  • lines 39–43: the error message, or otherwise the help message, translated along with their parameters;
  • lines 29–33: [:host] refers to the component element itself ([<app-champ-saisie>]). An element unknown to the browser is displayed “in-line”: it is converted into a block so that the classes applied by the parent ([col-sm-6]) take effect.

The title, first name, and last name fields, which are common to three forms. The parent passes the three fields from its signal-based form to this component:

docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// components/champ-captcha.ts - the CAPTCHA image and the input field
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A custom form control (FormValueControl, see champ-saisie.ts)
// which loads a CAPTCHA (GET /api/captcha) as soon as it is created. The parent:
//    - links the input to its form: [formField]="f.captcha";
//    - retrieves the component itself via viewChild(ChampCaptcha), so that
//      call its methods PUBLIQUES: captchaId(), and reload() after
//      each attempt, because an image is only used UNE once (the server
//      forgets it as soon as it has verified it).
//
// [innerHTML] + bypassSecurityTrustHtml: the image SVG is inserted exactly
// as is. It’s safe ICI because it’s generated by our server
// (svg-captcha library) and contains nothing that comes from a
// user—see Example 22.
// =========================================================================

import { Component, computed, inject, input, model, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { DomSanitizer } from '@angular/platform-browser';
import { FormValueControl, ValidationError } from '@angular/forms/signals';
import { TranslatePipe } from '@ngx-translate/core';
import { RdvMedecinsApi } from '../api/rdvmedecins.api';
import { Captcha } from '../api/types';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-champ-captcha',
  imports: [TranslatePipe],
  styles: `
    :host {
      display: block;
    }
  `,
  template: `
    <div class="mb-3">
      <label class="form-label" for="captcha">{{ 'CAPTCHA.LABEL' | translate }}</label>
      <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-3 mb-2">
        <div class="captcha-image" role="img" [attr.aria-label]="'CAPTCHA.IMAGE_ALT' | translate" [innerHTML]="svg()"></div>
        <a href="#" class="small" (click)="$event.preventDefault(); recharger()">{{ 'CAPTCHA.NEW_IMAGE' | translate }}</a>
      </div>
      <input id="captcha" type="text" maxlength="10" autocomplete="off" autocapitalize="off" spellcheck="false"
             class="form-control" [class.is-invalid]="erreur()" [value]="value()" (input)="saisir($event)">
      @if (erreur(); as e) {
        <div class="invalid-feedback">{{ e | translate }}</div>
      } @else {
        <div class="form-text">{{ 'CAPTCHA.HELP' | translate }}</div>
      }
    </div>
  `,
})
export class ChampCaptcha implements FormValueControl<string> {
  readonly value = model('');
  readonly errors = input<readonly ValidationError.WithOptionalFieldTree[]>([]);

  private readonly api = inject(RdvMedecinsApi);
  private readonly sanitizer = inject(DomSanitizer);
  private readonly captcha = signal<Captcha | null>(null);
  protected readonly svg = computed(() => this.sanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml(this.captcha()?.svg ?? ''));
  protected readonly erreur = computed(() => this.errors()[0]?.message);

  constructor() {
    this.recharger();
  }

   // a new image and an empty field
  async recharger(): Promise<void> {
    this.value.set('');
    try {
      this.captcha.set(await this.api.captcha());
    } catch {
      this.captcha.set(null); // server unreachable: the connection will fail with a plaintext message
    }
  }

   // the ID of the displayed image, to be sent with the response
  captchaId(): string {
    return this.captcha()?.id ?? '';
  }

  protected saisir(evenement: Event): void {
    this.value.set((evenement.target as HTMLInputElement).value);
  }
}

The CAPTCHA image and its input field: another custom form control.

  • line 61: an image is loaded as soon as the component is created;
  • lines 65–72: [recharger] is public: the login page calls it after each attempt, since an image is used only once;
  • lines 75–77: the ID of the displayed image, to be sent with the response;
  • line 37: the image SVG (example 22), with alternative text for screen readers;
  • line 40: [autocapitalize] and [spellcheck]: no automatic capitalization or spell-checking on a phone.

The parent page obtains this component via [viewChild(ChampCaptcha)] (example 13) to call its public methods.

import { afterNextRender, Component, ElementRef, input, output, signal, viewChild } from '@angular/core';

})
export class FenetreReservation {
  readonly horaire = input.required<string>(); // "8:00 - 8:20"
  readonly clients = input<readonly Personne[]>([]); // ADMIN / DOCTOR: patients to choose from
  readonly patient = input<string | null>(null); // USER: the patient is the patient themselves
  readonly envoiEnCours = input(false);

  readonly confirmer = output<number | null>();
  readonly fermer = output<void>();

  protected readonly idClient = signal<number | null>(null);
  private readonly liste = viewChild<ElementRef<HTMLSelectElement>>('liste');
  private readonly boutonConfirmer = viewChild.required<ElementRef<HTMLButtonElement>>('boutonConfirmer');

The slot reservation window. It does not communicate with the server: it receives what it displays and sends the user’s decision; it is the calendar page that performs the action.
