  • line 4: language selection;
  • line 40: a “Dr.” title that the server will reject; see [ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE];
  • line 43 and following: under each field, the first error; its message is a key, which the pipe [translate] translates. [?? '']: no error, no text;
  • line 71: the button is disabled during submission;
  • line 80: the general message, in the current language, with its parameters, followed by the status HTTP and the key, for clarification;
  • Line 88: the confirmation window.

Changing the language also re-translates error messages that have already been displayed: we’ve only kept the keys.

[npm start 25-erreurs-serveur]; logged in as admin, we submit the title “Dr,” a first name that’s too long, an empty last name, and an invalid username:

We start with a blank form: the title “Dr,” the first name “Jean,” and a blank last name. The server rejects the title and the last name; we then correct the title and enter a last name: the errors in these two fields disappear immediately, without having to resubmit. The general message remains displayed until the next submission:

A namesake (Alice DURAND already exists): the server returns a 409 response and flags the first name and last name fields. The username “martin,” which is already taken, is not flagged: the server stops at the first violated validation rule. We then switch to English: the messages already displayed are re-translated (the login bar, written in French, is not):

Also try editing the same record in two tabs: the second entry receives [ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE].

docs.title: 12. Conclusion
docs.text:
We wrote the client [Angular] for the application [RdvMedecins]. For the user, it provides the same pages as the HTML application from the [NestJS] course, and as the [Vue.js] client from the previous course; for the developer, everything has shifted:

  • the server no longer generates pages. It exposes a API JSON, whose contract (routes, body, codes, and error keys) was sufficient to write the client without ever reading its code. The server is, in fact, exactly the same as the client’s [Vue.js]: only its comments have changed;
  • the pages, language, formatting, messages, and navigation have shifted to the browser;
  • security, however, has not changed: it is still the server that authenticates (cookie [HttpOnly]), verifies roles and management rules, and decides what a patient is allowed to see. The client simply displays what the server sends it.

Readers who have followed both courses can compare the two frameworks on the same application. [Angular] requires more code and concepts (classes, decorators, dependency injection, observables), but it provides everything: a router, forms, the HTTP client, interceptors, and build tools—along with recommended best practices for using them. [Angular] applications therefore all look alike, which is valuable for large teams and long-term projects. [Vue.js] is lighter and more flexible. With signals, the two frameworks have actually become more similar: [signal], [computed], and [effect] from [Angular] mirror [ref], [computed], and [watchEffect] from [Vue.js].

The concepts covered in this course (components, signals, signal forms, dependency injection, router, HTTP client) are those found in any modern [Angular] application. For further reading:

  • the official documentation, https://angular.dev, and its interactive tutorial;
  • the tests: [Vitest], provided by default by [Angular CLI] for unit tests of components and services, and [Playwright] for end-to-end tests (the screenshots in this document were taken using this tool);
  • server-side rendering ([Angular SSR], command [ng add @angular/ssr]), which generates the first page on the server: this would partially mirror the architecture of the course [NestJS];
  • the course “An Example of an Angular Client/Server” / NestJS (2026), which examines both a client ([Angular]) and its server.

docs.title: 11. Deployment
docs.text:
In development, two servers work together: the [Angular] development server (the client) and the JSON server (the API). In production, there is only one:

1. Build the client. In the [rdvmedecins-angular] folder:

npm run build

The console displays:

> rdvmedecins-angular@1.0.0 build
> ng build

✔ Building...
Initial chunk files | Names               |  Raw size | Estimated transfer size
chunk-BruCX3rK.js   | -                   | 296.78 kB |                80.48 kB
styles-ESMYSIMF.css | styles              | 231.34 kB |                22.65 kB
main-ZNWESYGE.js    | main                | 127.41 kB |                31.39 kB

                    | Initial total       | 655.53 kB |               134.52 kB

Lazy chunk files    | Names               |  Raw size | Estimated transfer size
chunk-Bqr4p6qO.js   | mon-compte          |   4.67 kB |                 1.63 kB
chunk-C49XOFB2.js   | -                   |   3.57 kB |                 1.35 kB
chunk-CWV4x81-.js   | personne-formulaire |   3.41 kB |                 1.45 kB
chunk-as-RKsXq.js   | espace-patient      |   3.40 kB |                 1.44 kB
chunk-CjiMzAsS.js   | personnes           |   3.26 kB |                 1.34 kB
chunk-DdMjXUoQ.js   | inscription         |   3.10 kB |                 1.31 kB
chunk-v1pH7ChH.js   | erreur              | 842 bytes |               842 bytes
chunk-9nUFW6Uu.js   | -                   | 548 bytes |               548 bytes

Application bundle generation complete. [3.938 seconds]

Output location: .../rdvmedecins-angular/dist/rdvmedecins-angular

The [dist/rdvmedecins-angular/browser/] folder contains the entire application: a [index.html] page, a stylesheet, and optimized [JavaScript] files (the code from [Angular], the router, [ngx-translate]... and ours):

  • The initial files are downloaded at startup: approximately 135 KB once compressed by the server;
  • each page loaded on demand ([loadComponent]) has its own file, downloaded on the first visit;
  • the name of each file contains a hash of its contents ([main-ZNWESYGE.js]): a new version will have a different name, and a browser will never be able to cache an outdated version;
  • the compiler has verified the budgets set in [angular.json]: a warning would indicate that an application has become too large.

2. Upload it to the server. Copy CONTENU from the [dist/rdvmedecins-angular/browser/] folder to a [client/] folder at the root of the JSON server ([rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/client/index.html], [rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/client/main-ZNWESYGE.js]...), then restart the server. It displays:

[Nest] LOG [RdvMedecins] client Angular servi depuis .../rdvmedecins-nestjs-json/client
[Nest] LOG [RdvMedecins] serveur JSON démarré : http://localhost:8080/api

The complete application is now available at http://localhost:8080. The server serves the client’s files and returns [index.html] for any other URL outside of /api: reloading the /agenda page works (it is the client’s browser that displays it). For the curious reader, it is the [src/web/client-spa.ts] file on the server that performs this task.

3. In a real production environment, don’t forget the file [.env] on the server:

  • a long, random [JWT_SECRET];
  • an empty [CAPTCHA_TEST];
  • [COOKIE_SECURE=true] if the site is served via HTTPS (it must be: passwords are being transmitted);
  • [TRUST_PROXY=true] if the server is behind a proxy ([nginx]...), so that the attempt limit sees the clients’ actual IP address.

We then launch the compiled server: [npm run build], followed by [npm run start:prod].

docs.title: 2.1. Example 01: The Structure of an Angular Application
2.1.1. The package.json file
docs.text:
The file [package.json] in the examples folder declares the libraries used and the project commands:

{
  "name": "exemples-angular",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Les petits exemples du cours [Introduction étape par étape au framework Angular] - une seule installation pour tous",
  "private": true,
  "scripts": {
    "ng": "ng",
    "start": "ng serve",
    "build": "ng build"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@angular/common": "^22.2.0",
    "@angular/compiler": "^22.2.0",
    "@angular/core": "^22.2.0",
    "@angular/forms": "^22.2.0",
    "@angular/platform-browser": "^22.2.0",
    "@angular/router": "^22.2.0",
    "@ngx-translate/core": "^18.0.0",
    "bootstrap": "^5.3.8",
    "rxjs": "~7.8.0",
    "tslib": "^2.8.0"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@angular/build": "^22.2.0",
    "@angular/cli": "^22.2.0",
    "@angular/compiler-cli": "^22.2.0",
    "typescript": "~6.0.2"
  }
}

Let’s break down this file:

  • Lines 6–10: the project commands, launched by [npm run <nom>] (or [npm start] for the command [start]):
    • [npm start 05-ngmodel] launches [ng serve 05-ngmodel]: the development server for Example 05;
    • [npm run build 05-ngmodel] launches [ng build 05-ngmodel]: the production version of example 05, located in the [dist/05-ngmodel/] folder;
    • [npm run ng -- <arguments>] provides access to all commands in the [ng] tool;
  • Lines 11–22: the libraries required by the application in the browser: the [Angular] packages ([@angular/core], the core; [@angular/common], common tools, including the client HTTP; [@angular/forms], forms; [@angular/router], the router; [@angular/platform-browser], browser initialization; [@angular/compiler], the template compiler; [ngx-translate] for languages; [Bootstrap] for formatting, [RxJS] for observables, and [tslib], a small helper library used by the code generated by [TypeScript];
  • lines 23–28: the development tools: the command-line tool [ng] ([@angular/cli]), the [Angular] compiler ([@angular/compiler-cli]), the build tool ([@angular/build], which relies on [esbuild] and [Vite]), and the [TypeScript] compiler. These are not part of the application delivered to users.

The prefix [^] for a version ([^22.2.0]) allows [npm] to install a newer version of the same major version (22.x.y); the prefix [~] ([~6.0.2]) allows only fixes (6.0.x). All [@angular/...] packages must have the same version.

In a standard project, this file is created by the [ng new nom-du-projet] command, which generates a complete, ready-to-run [Angular] application. The examples in this course were written by hand so that twenty-five of them could be included in a single folder.

docs.title: 2.1.2. The file angular.json
docs.text:
[angular.json] describes the workspace: the applications it contains, and how to build and serve them. Its beginning, which describes Example 01:

{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/@angular/cli/lib/config/schema.json",
  "version": 1,
  "cli": {
    "packageManager": "npm",
    "analytics": false
  },
  "projects": {
    "01-premiere-application": {
      "projectType": "application",
      "root": "01-premiere-application",
      "sourceRoot": "01-premiere-application/src",
      "prefix": "app",
      "architect": {
        "build": {
          "builder": "@angular/build:application",
          "options": {
            "outputPath": "dist/01-premiere-application",
            "index": "01-premiere-application/src/index.html",
            "browser": "01-premiere-application/src/main.ts",
            "tsConfig": "01-premiere-application/tsconfig.app.json",
            "styles": [
              "node_modules/bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css"
            ]
          },
          "configurations": {
            "production": {
              "outputHashing": "all"
            },
            "development": {
              "optimization": false,
              "extractLicenses": false,
              "sourceMap": true
            }
          },
          "defaultConfiguration": "production"
        },
        "serve": {
          "builder": "@angular/build:dev-server",
          "options": {
            "proxyConfig": "proxy.conf.json"
          },
          "configurations": {
            "production": {
              "buildTarget": "01-premiere-application:build:production"
            },
            "development": {
              "buildTarget": "01-premiere-application:build:development"
            }
          },
          "defaultConfiguration": "development"
        }
      }
    },
  • lines 4–7: the settings for the [ng] tool (the package manager, with no usage statistics collection);
  • line 9: the project name, the one given to [ng serve] or [npm start];
  • lines 11–12: the project directory and the source directory;
  • Line 13: the prefix for component selectors ([app-root], [app-carte-medecin]...);
  • Lines 15–37: the application build ([ng build]):
    • line 16: the build tool;
    • line 18: the output folder;
    • lines 19–20: the application’s page HTML and its entry point [TypeScript];
    • line 21: the project configuration [TypeScript];
    • lines 22–24: the application’s global style sheets: here, the one for [Bootstrap];
    • lines 26–36: two configurations: [production] (optimized code; [outputHashing] includes a content hash in each file name) and [development] (readable code, with “source maps” that allow debugging of [TypeScript] in the browser). [ng build] uses the first one by default (line 36);
  • lines 38–52: the development server ([ng serve]):
    • line 41: the proxy file, which will only be used starting with Example 22: any request from the browser to an address beginning with [/api] is forwarded to the server JSON [RdvMedecins]. We’ll come back to this;
    • line 51: [ng serve] builds the application using the [development] configuration.

The other twenty-four examples are described in the same way later in the file (more than a thousand lines in total). A standard project, created by [ng new], contains only one.

docs.title: 2.1.3. The files tsconfig.json and tsconfig.app.json
docs.text:
The [TypeScript] configuration common to all examples:

{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "strict": true,
    "noImplicitOverride": true,
    "noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature": true,
    "noImplicitReturns": true,
    "noFallthroughCasesInSwitch": true,
    "noUnusedLocals": true,
    "noUnusedParameters": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "experimentalDecorators": true,
    "importHelpers": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "preserve"
  },
  "angularCompilerOptions": {
    "strictInjectionParameters": true,
    "strictInputAccessModifiers": true,
    "strictTemplates": true
  },
  "include": ["*/src/**/*.ts", "commun/**/*.ts"]
}
  • line 3: the strict mode of [TypeScript] (types rigorously checked, including [null] and [undefined]);
  • lines 4–9: additional checks; in particular, an unused variable or parameter is reported as an error;
  • line 12: [Angular] uses the decorators from [TypeScript] ([@Component], [@Injectable]...);
  • line 14: A JSON file can be imported as a module (Example 21);
  • lines 15–16: modern [JavaScript] code (ES2022) and modules processed by the build tool;
  • lines 18–22: checks specific to the [Angular] compiler. The most important one, on line 21: templates are checked as [TypeScript]. A typo in a template ([{{ titr }}] instead of [{{ titre }}]) results in a compilation error, reported by [ng serve] and by the editor;
  • Line 23: the files displayed by the editor ([VS Code]): those from all the examples.

Each example also has its own file, [tsconfig.app.json], which uses this configuration and compiles only the SES files:

{
  "extends": "../tsconfig.json",
  "include": ["src/**/*.ts"]
}

Thus, an error in one example does not prevent the others from working.

docs.title: 2.1.4. The index.html page
docs.text:
Each example has its own HTML page. The one for Example 01:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Exemple 01 - une première application</title>
   <!-- base href: the starting address for relative paths (see the router) -->
  <base href="/">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
</head>
<body>
   <!-- the Angular application is displayed in this element (see src/main.ts) -->
  <app-root></app-root>
</body>
</html>

This is the only page the browser will load. It is almost empty:

  • line 7: the base address for the page’s relative paths; the router (example 17) uses this;
  • line 12: the element in which [Angular] will display the application. This is not a known HTML tag: it is the selector for the application’s root component.

There are no [<script>] or [<link>] tags: the build tool adds them automatically (the compiled program, the [Bootstrap] stylesheet).

docs.title: 2.1.5. The entry point: main.ts
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 01-first-app/src/main.ts - the application’s entry point
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// angular.json designates this file as the entry point ("browser"). It
// launches the Angular application from its RACINE (App) component:
// Angular searches index.html for the <app-root> element (the "selector" for
// App) and displays the component’s HTML there.
// =========================================================================

import { bootstrapApplication } from '@angular/platform-browser';
import { App } from './app/app';

// bootstrapApplication(App) returns a promise: any
// startup error in the browser console
bootstrapApplication(App).catch((erreur) => console.error(erreur));
  • Line 10: the function in [Angular] that launches an application in a browser;
  • line 11: the root component of the application, the [App] class from the [app/app.ts] file;
  • line 15: the application is launched from this component: [Angular] searches the page for the element [<app-root>] and displays the HTML from [App] there.

docs.title: 2.1.6. The root component: app.ts, app.html, app.css
docs.text:
A component [Angular] is a class [TypeScript] decorated by [@Component]:

// =========================================================================
// 01-first-application/src/app/app.ts - a first component
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// An Angular component is a CLASSE TypeScript, decorated with @Component:
//    - selecto   r : the HTML tag that represents it (<app-root>);
//    - templateUrl: the sound file HTML (app.html);
//    - styleUr   l : the sound file CSS (app.css), which applies
//                    to this component.
// The class’s properties and methods can be used in the template.
// =========================================================================

import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  templateUrl: './app.html',
  styleUrl: './app.css',
})
export class App {
   // "Ordinary" data: the template can display it
  protected readonly titre = 'Bienvenue dans Angular';
  protected readonly langages = ['TypeScript', 'HTML', 'CSS'];

   // signal(...): a RÉACTIVE data item. Its value is read via the APPELANT
   // (counter()), and it is changed using set() or update(). Angular then updates
   // AUTOMATIQUEMENT to the parts of the page that display it.
  protected readonly compteur = signal(0);
  protected readonly heure = signal(new Date().toLocaleTimeString());

   // a method called by the button in the template
  protected incrementer(): void {
    this.compteur.update((n) => n + 1);
    this.heure.set(new Date().toLocaleTimeString());
  }
}
  • Lines 14–18: The [@Component] decorator turns the class into a component:
    • line 15: its selector, the tag that represents it in a template or in [index.html];
    • line 16: its template file, HTML;
    • line 17: its style file, CSS;
  • lines 21–22: two ordinary data items. [protected]: they are used only by the component and its template; [readonly]: they will not be replaced;
  • line 27: [signal(0)] creates a reactive data point with an initial value of 0. A signal is a function: you read its value by calling it ([this.compteur()]), and you change it using [set(valeur)] or [update(fonction)]. When it changes, [Angular] updates all locations on the page that display it;
  • lines 31–34: a method that modifies two signals. It does not alter the page: [Angular] will update it. [update((n) => n + 1)] calculates the new value based on the old one.

The component’s template:

<!-- 01-first-application/src/app/app.html—the App component’s template -->
<div class="container py-4">
   <!-- {{ expression }}: the value of the expression, inserted into the page -->
  <h1 class="h3">{{ titre }}</h1>
  <p>Cette page est fabriquée dans le navigateur, par Angular, à partir de index.html, main.ts et du composant App.</p>
  <p>On y écrit du {{ langages.join(', ') }} ({{ langages.length }} langages).</p>

   <!-- (click): the method to call when clicked (see example 04) -->
  <button class="btn btn-primary" (click)="incrementer()">Cliquez-moi</button>
   <!-- A signal is read by calling it: counter(), not counter -->
  <p class="mt-3 compteur">Vous avez cliqué {{ compteur() }} fois (dernier clic : {{ heure() }}).</p>
</div>
  • Line 4: The syntax [{{ expression }}] (interpolation) inserts into the page the value of an expression [TypeScript], evaluated on the component ([titre] refers to [this.titre]). It is escaped: if [titre] contained [<b>], [<b>] would be displayed, without the tag being interpreted;
  • line 6: the expression can be anything: a method call, a calculation;
  • line 9: Clicking the button calls the method [incrementer] (see Example 04);
  • line 11: a signal is displayed when the method is called: [{{ compteur() }}]. [Angular] notes that the template reads this signal: when it changes, this part of the page will be updated.

And its style:

/* this rule applies only to elements of the App component */
.compteur {
  font-weight: bold;
  color: #dd0031;
}

This rule applies only to elements of the CE component: [Angular] adds a unique attribute to its elements ([_ngcontent-xxx]) and passes it on to the CSS selectors. This is style encapsulation: two components can use the same CSS class without interfering with each other.

A component can also write its template and style directly in the decorator, using the properties [template] and [styles] instead of [templateUrl] and [styleUrl]. The following examples will demonstrate this for small components.

docs.title: 2.1.7. Execution
docs.text:
In the console open to the [exemples-angular] folder:

npm start 01-premiere-application

The console displays (excerpt):

Initial chunk files | Names         |  Raw size
styles.css          | styles        | 276.99 kB |
main.js             | main          |   5.06 kB |

Application bundle generation complete. [1.653 seconds]

Watch mode enabled. Watching for file changes...
  ➜  Local:   http://localhost:4200/

Open the URL http://localhost:4200/ and click the button three times:

Two experiments to try:

  • Change the title text in [app.ts] and save the file: the page updates immediately, without having to reload it. The development server monitors the files, recompiles the changes, and notifies the browser;
  • view the page’s source code (Ctrl-U): you’ll only see the [index.html] page, which is almost empty. The HTML page displayed was generated by [Angular] within the browser. To view it, use the developer tools inspector (F12, Elements tab) or the [Angular DevTools] extension, which also displays the components and their data.

docs.title: 2.2. Example 02: Signals
docs.text:
Signals are at the heart of [Angular]’s responsiveness. This example calculates the price TTC of an item:

// =========================================================================
// 02-signals/src/app/app.ts - signal, computed, effect, linkedSignal
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A small price calculator TTC:
//    - signa      l : a reactive value, which is read by calling it and
//                     which is modified using set() / update();
//    - compute    d : a value CALCULÉE derived from other signals,
//                     automatically recalculated when they change;
//    - effec      t : code executed whenever the signals it
//                     reads (a “side effect”);
//    - linkedSignal: a modifiable signal, but REMIS with a value calculated
//                     when another signal changes.
// =========================================================================

import { Component, computed, effect, linkedSignal, signal, untracked } from '@angular/core';
// FormsModule provides [(ngModel)], which links a field to a signal (see example 05)
import { FormsModule } from '@angular/forms';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  imports: [FormsModule],
  templateUrl: './app.html',
})
export class App {
  protected readonly libelle = signal('Stylo');
  protected readonly prixHT = signal(2.5);
  protected readonly tauxTVA = signal(20); // as a percentage

   // linkedSignal: the quantity resets to 1 every time the item changes,
   // but the user can modify it in the meantime
  protected readonly quantite = linkedSignal({ source: this.libelle, computation: () => 1 });

   // computed: never assigned directly, always recalculated. Angular knows
   // which signals it depends on (the ones it LIT): it recalculates it when one
   // of them changes, and only in that case
  protected readonly totalHT = computed(() => this.quantite() * this.prixHT());
  protected readonly montantTVA = computed(() => (this.totalHT() * this.tauxTVA()) / 100);
  protected readonly totalTTC = computed(() => this.totalHT() + this.montantTVA());

   // a euro amount formatter, in the French style (1,234.50 €)
  private readonly euros = new Intl.NumberFormat('fr-FR', { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' });

   // the history of totals TTC, populated by the effect below
  protected readonly historique = signal<string[]>([]);
  private ancienTTC: number | null = null;

  constructor() {
     // effect: executed once, then each time
     // totalTTC (the only signal it reads)
    effect(() => {
      const ttc = this.totalTTC();
      document.title = `TTC : ${this.format(ttc)}`;
      if (this.ancienTTC !== null) {
        const ligne = `${this.format(this.ancienTTC)} -> ${this.format(ttc)}`;
         // untracked: modify history SANS to make it a dependency of the effect
        untracked(() => this.historique.update((h) => [ligne, ...h].slice(0, 5)));
      }
      this.ancienTTC = ttc;
    });
  }

  protected format(montant: number): string {
    return this.euros.format(montant);
  }

  protected reinitialiser(): void {
    this.libelle.set('Stylo');
    this.prixHT.set(2.5);
    this.tauxTVA.set(20);
    this.quantite.set(1);
  }
}
  • line 15: the responsiveness functions, all provided by [@angular/core];
  • Lines 21 and 17: The template uses [[(ngModel)]], which comes from the [FormsModule] module. A component must import (array [imports]) everything its template uses: other components, directives, and pipes. The compiler reports an error if this is omitted;
  • lines 25–27: three signals, [signal(valeur initiale)]. Their type is inferred from the initial value: [signal('Stylo')] is a string signal, [signal(2.5)] is a numeric signal;
  • line 31: a [linkedSignal] is a modifiable signal (it can be written to, just like an ordinary signal), but it is linked to another signal, its source: whenever the source changes (in this case, the item description), its value is reset to the value calculated by [computation] (in this case, 1). When the item changes, the quantity resets to 1;
  • lines 36–38: a [computed] is a value calculated from other signals. It is never written; it is read as a signal ([this.totalHT()]). [Angular] knows which signals it depends on, because it records the ones the function reads during the calculation. It is recalculated when one of them changes, and only in that case: reading [totalTTC()] ten times without anything changing results in only a single calculation. A [computed] may depend on other [computed] values (line 38);
  • line 41: a French-style amount formatter (1,234.50 €). Example 09 will show how to do this with [Angular], the pipes;
  • lines 50–59: a [effect] is a function executed once, then each time the signals it reads change (here, the single [totalTTC]). This is used for side effects: performing actions on something other than the page (the tab title, line 52; the browser’s local storage; a log);
    • line 56: the effect adds an entry to the history. [untracked(...)] performs this update without making [historique] a dependency of the effect; otherwise, the effect would read [historique] (in [update]) and would be re-triggered every time the history changes... which it itself causes;
    • A [effect] is created in the component’s constructor (or when a property is initialized): this is what [Angular] calls the injection context, which we’ll discuss further when covering services (Example 14). It stops on its own when the component is destroyed;
  • Lines 66–71: [set()] replaces the value of a signal. The quantity is a [linkedSignal]: it can be written just like the others.

Avoid writing into a signal using a [effect] when a [computed] is sufficient: a [computed] describes a value, while a [effect] describes an action. Here, the history depends on the successive values of the total, which a [computed] cannot express.

The template:

<div class="container py-4">
  <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 02 - les signaux</h1>
  <div class="row g-4">
    <div class="col-md-6">
      <div class="card p-3">
         <!-- [(ngModel)]="signal": the field reads the signal and modifies it (see example 05) -->
        <label class="form-label" for="libelle">Article</label>
        <input id="libelle" class="form-control mb-2" [(ngModel)]="libelle">
        <label class="form-label" for="prix">Prix unitaire HT</label>
        <input id="prix" type="number" step="0.1" min="0" class="form-control mb-2" [(ngModel)]="prixHT">
        <label class="form-label" for="quantite">Quantité (revient à 1 si l'article change)</label>
        <input id="quantite" type="number" min="0" class="form-control mb-2" [(ngModel)]="quantite">
        <label class="form-label" for="tva">Taux de TVA</label>
        <select id="tva" class="form-select mb-3" [(ngModel)]="tauxTVA">
           <!-- [ngValue]: the value passed is NOMBRE 5.5, not the string "5.5" -->
          <option [ngValue]="5.5">5,5 %</option>
          <option [ngValue]="10">10 %</option>
          <option [ngValue]="20">20 %</option>
        </select>
        <button class="btn btn-outline-secondary" (click)="reinitialiser()">Réinitialiser</button>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="col-md-6">
      <div class="card p-3">
        <h2 class="h5">{{ quantite() }} x {{ libelle() }}</h2>
        <table class="table mb-0">
          <tbody>
            <tr><td>Total HT</td><td class="text-end">{{ format(totalHT()) }}</td></tr>
            <tr><td>TVA ({{ tauxTVA() }} %)</td><td class="text-end">{{ format(montantTVA()) }}</td></tr>
            <tr class="fw-bold"><td>Total TTC</td><td class="text-end">{{ format(totalTTC()) }}</td></tr>
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
      <div class="card p-3 mt-3">
        <h2 class="h6">Historique du total TTC (effect)</h2>
        <ul class="mb-0">
          @for (ligne of historique(); track $index) {
            <li>{{ ligne }}</li>
          }
        </ul>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
  • lines 8–18: [[(ngModel)]="libelle"] links the field to the signal [libelle] in both directions: typing in the field changes the signal, and changing the signal (using the “Reset” button) changes the field. We specify the signal itself, without parentheses: [ngModel] requires the signal in order to write it. Example 05 will cover [ngModel] in detail;
  • lines 10 and 12: with [type="number"], the signal receives a number, not a string;
  • lines 16–18: [[ngValue]] provides the value of an option: in this case, the number 5.5, not the string ["5.5"];
  • lines 25–30: the display of signals and [computed]. [format(...)] is a method of the component;
  • lines 37–39: [@for] repeats the block for each item in a list (see Example 03).

With the development server running ([npm start 02-signaux]), we modify the item, price, quantity, and rate:

Each time the total changes (TTC), the effect adds a line to the history and changes the tab title. Changing the item resets the quantity to 1.

These signals are not specific to [Angular]: they are also found in [SolidJS], [Preact], [Vue.js] (where [ref] serves the same purpose), and a draft standard proposes adding them to [JavaScript] itself. Before signals (introduced in [Angular] 16, in 2023), [Angular] regularly checked the entire component tree, using the [zone.js] library, to determine what had changed. With signals, it knows exactly what to update: this is the “zoneless” mode, which is the default in [Angular] 22 and is used in all the examples in this course.

docs.title: 2.3. Example 03: Template Syntax
docs.text:
A [Angular] template is HTML enhanced with a few syntax elements. This example displays a list of doctors that can be filtered:

// =========================================================================
// 03-templates/src/app/app.ts - template syntax
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// In an Angular template:
//    - [propriete]="expr ": a property of the element, calculated by an
//                            expression ([src], [disabled], [hidden]...);
//    - [class.nom]="expr ": the class CSS "name" if the expression is true;
//      [style.prop]="expr": a CSS property;
//    - @if / @else if / @else: a block that exists only if the condition
//                            is true;
//    - @for (x of list; track x.id): a block repeated for each element;
//      track returns the IDENTITÉ of each element; @empty, the block is displayed
//      when the list is empty;
//    - @switch / @cas    e : one block among several, depending on a value;
//    - @let name = exp   r; : a variable local to the template.
// =========================================================================

import { Component, computed, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { FormsModule } from '@angular/forms';

// an interface TypeScript describes the format of the objects in the list
interface Medecin {
  id: number;
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
  specialite: 'généraliste' | 'pédiatre' | 'cardiologue';
  disponible: boolean;
}

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  imports: [FormsModule],
  templateUrl: './app.html',
})
export class App {
   // The image is in the example's public/ folder: served as-is
  protected readonly urlLogo = 'medecin.svg';

  protected readonly medecins = signal<Medecin[]>([
    { id: 1, titre: 'Mme', prenom: 'Marie', nom: 'PELISSIER', specialite: 'généraliste', disponible: true },
    { id: 2, titre: 'Mr', prenom: 'Paul', nom: 'TATOU', specialite: 'pédiatre', disponible: false },
    { id: 3, titre: 'Melle', prenom: 'Sophie', nom: 'DUPONT', specialite: 'cardiologue', disponible: true },
  ]);

  protected readonly filtre = signal(''); // search text
  protected readonly seulementDisponibles = signal(false);
  protected readonly afficherAide = signal(true);

   // The displayed list: a computed field, recalculated when the filter changes
  protected readonly medecinsAffiches = computed(() => {
    const texte = this.filtre().trim().toLowerCase();
    return this.medecins().filter(
      (m) =>
        (!this.seulementDisponibles() || m.disponible) &&
        `${m.prenom} ${m.nom} ${m.specialite}`.toLowerCase().includes(texte),
    );
  });

  protected basculerAide(): void {
    this.afficherAide.update((a) => !a);
  }
}
  • lines 22–29: a [TypeScript] interface describes the format of the objects in the list. The specialty can only take three values (line 27);
  • line 38: the address of an image. The files in the example’s [public/] folder are served as-is, at the root of the site: [medecin.svg] refers to the file [03-templates/public/medecin.svg]. To do this, you must declare it in [angular.json]:
            "assets": [
              {
                "glob": "**/*",
                "input": "03-templates/public"
              }
            ]
  • lines 40–44: [signal<Medecin[]>(...)]: a signal whose type is specified, a list of doctors;
  • lines 46–48: three signals linked to the page’s fields;
  • lines 51–58: the displayed list, a [computed] that depends on four signals ([filtre], [medecins], [seulementDisponibles]);
  • line 61: [update] inverts a Boolean.

The template:

<div class="container py-4">
  <h1 class="h3 mb-3">
     <!-- [src]: the value of the src property is that of urlLogo -->
    <img [src]="urlLogo" alt="logo" width="32" height="32">
    Exemple 03 - la syntaxe des templates
  </h1>

  <div class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-3 align-items-center mb-3">
    <input class="form-control w-auto" placeholder="rechercher..." [(ngModel)]="filtre">
    <label class="form-check-label">
      <input type="checkbox" class="form-check-input" [(ngModel)]="seulementDisponibles"> disponibles seulement
    </label>
    <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" (click)="basculerAide()">
      {{ afficherAide() ? "Cacher l'aide" : "Montrer l'aide" }}
    </button>
  </div>

   <!-- [hidden]: the paragraph remains on the page, but is simply hidden -->
  <p class="alert alert-info" [hidden]="!afficherAide()">
    Tapez un nom ou une spécialité. Les médecins indisponibles sont grisés.
  </p>

   <!-- @let: a template variable, to avoid repeating the call -->
  @let affiches = medecinsAffiches();

   <!-- @if / @else if / @else: only one of the three blocks exists at a time -->
  @if (medecins().length === 0) {
    <p class="text-muted">Aucun médecin.</p>
  } @else if (affiches.length === 0) {
    <p class="text-warning">Aucun médecin ne correspond à « {{ filtre() }} ».</p>
  } @else {
    <table class="table">
      <thead>
        <tr><th>#</th><th>Doctor</th><th>Specialty</th><th>Status</th></tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
         <!-- @for: one row per doctor; $index specifies the rank.
             track m.id : l'identité de chaque ligne, pour qu'Angular sache
             quelle ligne ajouter, déplacer ou supprimer quand la liste change -->
        @for (m of affiches; track m.id; let i = $index) {
          <tr [class.opacity-50]="!m.disponible">
            <td>{{ i + 1 }}</td>
            <td>{{ m.titre }} {{ m.prenom }} {{ m.nom }}</td>
            <td>
               <!-- @switch: one block depending on the specialty value -->
              @switch (m.specialite) {
                @case ('pédiatre') { <span title="enfants">🧸</span> }
                @case ('cardiologue') { <span title="cœur">❤️</span> }
                @default { <span title="tous publics">🩺</span> }
              }
              {{ m.specialite }}
            </td>
            <td>
               <!-- [class] with a string: the calculated classes are added to "badge" -->
              <span class="badge" [class]="m.disponible ? 'text-bg-success' : 'text-bg-secondary'">
                {{ m.disponible ? 'disponible' : 'indisponible' }}
              </span>
            </td>
          </tr>
        }
      </tbody>
    </table>
  }

   <!-- [style.font-size.px]: a property CSS, with its unit -->
  <p [style.font-size.px]="12 + affiches.length * 2">
    {{ affiches.length }} médecin(s) affiché(s) - la taille de ce texte en dépend.
  </p>
</div>
  • Line 4: [[src]="urlLogo"] is a property binding: the property [src] of the element is assigned the value of the expression [urlLogo]. Without the square brackets, [src="urlLogo"] would result in the string ["urlLogo"]. Any property of an element can be bound in this way: [[disabled]], [[value]], [[hidden]], [[title]]...;
  • lines 9 and 11: two fields linked to signals via [[(ngModel)]] (see Example 05);
  • line 14: interpolation supports the ternary operator [? :];
  • line 19: [[hidden]]: the paragraph remains on the page, but is simply hidden (property HTML [hidden]);
  • line 24: [@let] declares a template variable, which is visible throughout the rest of the template. This avoids having to repeat [medecinsAffiches()];
  • lines 27–63: [@if (condition) { ... } @else if (...) { ... } @else { ... }]: only one of the three blocks exists on the page at a time. Unlike [[hidden]], the elements of a block that is not selected are not created (or are removed);
  • line 40: [@for (m of affiches; track m.id)] repeats the block for each doctor:
    • [track m.id] is required: it identifies each row. When the list changes, [Angular] compares the identifiers to determine which row to add, move, or delete, rather than recreating everything. For a list of simple values without an identifier, write [track $index] (example 02);
    • [let i = $index]: the element’s rank. [@for] also provides [$first], [$last], [$even], [$odd], and [$count];
    • a block labeled [@empty { ... }], following the block labeled [@for], appears when the list is empty (example 16);
  • line 41: [[class.opacity-50]="condition"]: the class [opacity-50] (from [Bootstrap]) is applied to the element if the condition is true;
  • lines 46–50: [@switch] selects a block based on a value: one [@case] per value, and [@default] for the others;
  • line 55: [[class]="expression"]: the expression returns one or more classes, which are added to the hard-coded classes ([badge]);
  • line 66: [[style.font-size.px]="expression"]: a property CSS, with its unit.

A template expression resembles [TypeScript], but it is restricted: no assignments (except in event handlers, example 04), no [new], no access to global variables ([window], [document]). It can only access the component’s properties and methods.

[npm start 03-templates]:

Type “gen” and hide the help:

Earlier versions of [Angular] wrote these blocks using structural directives: [*ngIf], [*ngFor], [[ngSwitch]]. They are still found in many projects; the syntax [@if] / [@for] / [@switch], which was introduced with [Angular] 17, is now recommended.

docs.title: 2.4. Example 04: Events
docs.text:
A list of tasks to respond to user actions. The component:

// =========================================================================
// 04-events/src/app/app.ts - respond to user actions
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// (event)="instruction": the instruction is executed when the element
// emits this event:
//    - (click)="f()           " calls f;
//    - (click)="f(3, $event)  " calls f with arguments; $event is
//                               the browser’s native event;
//    - (keyup.enter), (keydown.escape): only for this key;
//    - #name on an element: a "reference variable" of the template, which
//      refers to the HTML element itself (nom.value, nom.focus()...).
// Here, there is no FormsModule or ngModel: we read the fields ourselves.
// =========================================================================

import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core';

interface Tache {
  id: number;
  libelle: string;
  faite: boolean;
}

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  templateUrl: './app.html',
  styles: `
    .zone {
      background: #e9f2ff;
      height: 80px;
      cursor: crosshair;
    }
  `,
})
export class App {
  protected readonly taches = signal<Tache[]>([
    { id: 1, libelle: 'Installer Node.js', faite: true },
    { id: 2, libelle: 'Lire le chapitre sur les événements', faite: false },
  ]);
  protected readonly journal = signal<string[]>([]);
  private prochainId = 3;

  private tracer(message: string): void {
    this.journal.update((j) => [`${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()} ${message}`, ...j]);
  }

   // called by (submit): $event.preventDefault() prevents the browser
   // from submitting the form to the server (and reloading the page)
  protected ajouter(evenement: SubmitEvent, champ: HTMLInputElement): void {
    evenement.preventDefault();
    const libelle = champ.value.trim();
    if (libelle === '') {
      return;
    }
     // a signal containing an array: it is REMPLACE by a new array
    this.taches.update((t) => [...t, { id: this.prochainId++, libelle, faite: false }]);
    this.tracer(`ajout de « ${libelle} »`);
    champ.value = '';
    champ.focus();
  }

  protected basculer(tache: Tache, faite: boolean): void {
    this.taches.update((t) => t.map((x) => (x.id === tache.id ? { ...x, faite } : x)));
    this.tracer(`« ${tache.libelle} » : ${faite ? 'faite' : 'à faire'}`);
  }

  protected supprimer(tache: Tache): void {
    this.taches.update((t) => t.filter((x) => x.id !== tache.id));
    this.tracer(`suppression de « ${tache.libelle} »`);
  }

   // $event: the native event (in this case, a MouseEvent), along with its coordinates
  protected position(evenement: MouseEvent): void {
    this.tracer(`clic en (${evenement.offsetX}, ${evenement.offsetY})`);
  }
}
  • lines 26–32: the component’s style, written directly in the decorator ([styles]), rather than in a [.css] file;
  • lines 35–38: a signal containing a list of objects;
  • line 40: a regular property, which is not displayed: it does not need to be a signal;
  • lines 48–59: adding a task. The method receives the event from the browser and the [<input>] element itself (see the template):
    • line 49: [preventDefault()] prevents the browser from submitting the form to the server, which would reload the page;
    • line 55: the array contained in the signal ([push]) is not modified; instead, it is replaced with a new array. A signal only indicates a change if its value changes—that is, if a AUTRE object is assigned to it. Modifying the contents of the array without replacing it would leave the page unchanged;
    • lines 57–58: the field is cleared and retains focus;
  • line 62: same principle for modifying a task: [map] creates a new array, where the task in question is replaced by a modified copy ([{ ...x, faite }]);
  • line 67: and to delete one, [filter];
  • Lines 72–74: [MouseEvent]: the click event, with the pointer position.

The template:

<div class="container py-4">
  <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 04 - les événements</h1>

   <!-- (submit): Entry in the OU field; click on the button.
        #new: a reference to the <input> element, usable anywhere
       dans le template -->
  <form class="d-flex gap-2 mb-3" (submit)="ajouter($event, nouvelle)">
    <input #new class="form-control" placeholder="new task (Esc to clear)"
           (keydown.escape)="nouvelle.value = ''">
    <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Ajouter</button>
  </form>

  <ul class="list-group mb-3">
    @for (t of taches(); track t.id) {
      <li class="list-group-item d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
         <!-- #case: the checkbox for the CETTE row; case.checked: its status -->
        <input #checkbox type="checkbox" class="form-check-input" [checked]="t.faite"
               (change)="basculer(t, case.checked)">
        <span class="flex-grow-1" [class.text-decoration-line-through]="t.faite" [class.text-muted]="t.faite">
          {{ t.libelle }}
        </span>
         <!-- a handler with an argument: the task for the CETTE line -->
        <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger" (click)="supprimer(t)">Supprimer</button>
      </li>
    }
  </ul>

  <div class="zone p-3 mb-3 rounded" (click)="position($event)">Cliquez dans cette zone</div>

  <h2 class="h6">Journal</h2>
  <ul class="small">
    @for (ligne of journal(); track $index) {
      <li>{{ ligne }}</li>
    }
  </ul>
</div>
  • line 7: [(submit)="instruction"] is an event binding: the instruction is executed when the element triggers the event [submit] (field input or button click). [$event] refers to the browser event;
  • Line 8: [#nouvelle] is a template reference variable: it refers to the [<input>] element itself, throughout the entire template. On line 7, it is passed to the [ajouter] method;
  • Line 9: [(keydown.escape)]: the [keydown] event, but only for the Esc key. Similarly, we write [(keyup.enter)], [(keydown.control.s)]... In an event binding, assignment is allowed: [nouvelle.value = ''] clears the field;
  • lines 17–18: [#case] refers to the checkbox associated with CETTE on the [@for] line; [[checked]] checks the box based on the task; [(change)] notifies the component when the user changes it;
  • Line 23: a handler with an argument: the task for this line;
  • line 28: a click in the field: [$event] is a [MouseEvent].

Here, we read the fields ourselves ([champ.value], [case.checked]). The following examples will delegate this task to [ngModel] and then to signal-based forms.

[npm start 04-evenements]; add a task (Input), check the second one, and click in the field:

[Angular] updates the page only in response to an event or a signal change. An event handled by the template ((click), (submit), etc.) is sufficient to trigger a check of the component; however, data modified later—outside of an event (such as in response to a server or when a timer ticks)—will only be displayed if it is a signal. Hence the rule followed throughout this course: any data displayed by a template is a signal.

docs.title: 2.5. Example 05: Form Fields and ngModel
docs.text:
The same form as Example 18 from the [NestJS] course (all field types), but without a server: everything happens in the browser. The fields are linked to signals via the [ngModel] directive:

// =========================================================================
// 05-ngmodel/src/app/app.ts - all field types, linked by ngModel
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// [(ngModel)]="signal" (module FormsModule) links a form field to a
// signal, in the sense that typing in the field modifies the signal, and
// modifying the signal (via code) changes the field. The syntax [( )], known as
// "banana in a box," combines [ngModel] (the signal to the field) and
// (ngModelChange) (the field to the signal). The value received depends on the field:
//    - text input, textarea          -> string
//    - input type="number           " -> number (null if the field is empty)
//    - checkbox only             -> boolean
//    - radio button                 s -> the value of the selected button
//    - select / select multipl      e -> the value / an array of values
//    - input type="date             " -> string "yyyy-MM-dd"
// In a <form>, each field linked by ngModel must have a "name" attribute.
// Same form as Example 18 in the NestJS course; but here, there is no
// server: everything happens in the browser.
// =========================================================================

import { Component, computed, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { JsonPipe } from '@angular/common';
import { FormsModule } from '@angular/forms';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
   // JsonPipe: the JSON “pipe,” which displays an object in the format JSON (see Example 09)
  imports: [FormsModule, JsonPipe],
  templateUrl: './app.html',
})
export class App {
  protected readonly titres = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
  protected readonly loisirsPossibles = ['sport', 'musique', 'lecture', 'cinéma'];
  protected readonly listePays = [
    { code: 'fr', libelle: 'France' },
    { code: 'be', libelle: 'Belgique' },
    { code: 'ch', libelle: 'Suisse' },
  ];

   // a signal for each form field
  protected readonly titre = signal('Mme');
  protected readonly nom = signal('');
  protected readonly age = signal<number | null>(30);
  protected readonly presentation = signal('');
  protected readonly newsletter = signal(false);
  protected readonly loisirs = signal<string[]>(['lecture']);
  protected readonly pays = signal('fr');
  protected readonly langues = signal<string[]>([]);
  protected readonly naissance = signal('');

   // all values, combined into a single object (what would be sent to a server)
  protected readonly modele = computed(() => ({
    titre: this.titre(),
    nom: this.nom().trim(), // ngModel does not remove spaces: we do that here
    age: this.age(),
    presentation: this.presentation(),
    newsletter: this.newsletter(),
    loisirs: this.loisirs(),
    pays: this.pays(),
    langues: this.langues(),
    naissance: this.naissance(),
  }));

  protected readonly envoye = signal<string | null>(null);

   // multiple checkboxes for UN table: ngModel can’t handle this, so we take care of it
  protected basculerLoisir(loisir: string, coche: boolean): void {
    this.loisirs.update((l) => (coche ? [...l, loisir] : l.filter((x) => x !== loisir)));
  }

   // (ngSubmit): Submit the form without reloading the page
  protected envoyer(): void {
    this.envoye.set(JSON.stringify(this.modele()));
  }
}
  • Line 22: [FormsModule] includes the [ngModel] directive (as well as [ngSubmit], [ngModelOptions]...): these are the so-called “template-driven” forms ([template-driven forms]);
  • line 27: the component also imports the [json] pipe, which displays an object in the JSON format (see example 09);
  • lines 40–48: one signal per field, with the type of value the field will provide: a string, a number (or [null] if the field is empty), a Boolean, or a list of strings;
  • lines 51–61: all values, grouped into a single object using [computed]: this is what would be sent to a server. [ngModel] does not remove spaces around an entry: we do that here (line 53);
  • lines 66–68: multiple checkboxes for the same list: [ngModel] cannot handle this, so we take care of it;
  • lines 71–73: the submission.

The template:

<div class="container py-4">
  <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 05 - les champs d'un formulaire et ngModel</h1>
  <div class="row g-4">
     <!-- (ngSubmit): with FormsModule, the form is never submitted to the
         serveur par le navigateur ; c'est notre méthode qui est appelée -->
    <form class="col-md-7" (ngSubmit)="envoyer()">
      <div class="mb-3">
        <span class="form-label d-block">Titre</span>
         <!-- radio buttons: same as ngModel, one value per button -->
        @for (t of titres; track t) {
          <div class="form-check form-check-inline">
            <input type="radio" class="form-check-input" name="titre" [id]="'titre-' + t" [value]="t"
                   [(ngModel)]="titre">
            <label class="form-check-label" [for]="'titre-' + t">{{ t }}</label>
          </div>
        }
      </div>
      <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
        <div class="col-8">
          <label class="form-label" for="nom">Nom</label>
          <input id="nom" name="nom" class="form-control" [(ngModel)]="nom">
        </div>
        <div class="col-4">
          <label class="form-label" for="age">Âge</label>
           <!-- type="number": the event receives a number, not the string "30" -->
          <input id="age" name="age" type="number" class="form-control" [(ngModel)]="age">
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="mb-3">
        <label class="form-label" for="presentation">Présentation (mise à jour à la sortie du champ)</label>
         <!-- updateOn: 'blur': the signal is only updated when the field is exited -->
        <textarea id="presentation" name="presentation" rows="2" class="form-control"
                  [(ngModel)]="presentation" [ngModelOptions]="{ updateOn: 'blur' }"></textarea>
      </div>
      <div class="mb-3 form-check">
         <!-- a single checkbox: true / false -->
        <input id="newsletter" name="newsletter" type="checkbox" class="form-check-input" [(ngModel)]="newsletter">
        <label for="newsletter" class="form-check-label">Recevoir la lettre d'information</label>
      </div>
      <div class="mb-3">
        <span class="form-label d-block">Loisirs</span>
         <!-- multiple checkboxes for the same table: [checked] + (change) -->
        @for (l of loisirsPossibles; track l) {
          <div class="form-check form-check-inline">
            <input #caseLoisir type="checkbox" class="form-check-input" [id]="'leisure-' + l"
                   [checked]="loisirs().includes(l)" (change)="basculerLoisir(l, caseLoisir.checked)">
            <label class="form-check-label" [for]="'loisir-' + l">{{ l }}</label>
          </div>
        }
      </div>
      <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
        <div class="col-6">
          <label class="form-label" for="pays">Pays</label>
          <select id="pays" name="pays" class="form-select" [(ngModel)]="pays">
             <!-- [value]: the value transmitted (the code), with the displayed text being the label -->
            @for (p of listePays; track p.code) {
              <option [value]="p.code">{{ p.libelle }}</option>
            }
          </select>
        </div>
        <div class="col-6">
          <label class="form-label" for="langues">Langues parlées</label>
          <select id="langues" name="langues" multiple size="3" class="form-select" [(ngModel)]="langues">
            <option value="fr">français</option>
            <option value="en">anglais</option>
            <option value="es">espagnol</option>
          </select>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="mb-3">
        <label class="form-label" for="naissance">Date de naissance</label>
        <input id="naissance" name="naissance" type="date" class="form-control w-auto" [(ngModel)]="naissance">
      </div>
      <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Envoyer</button>
    </form>

    <div class="col-md-5">
      <h2 class="h6">Le modèle, en direct</h2>
      <pre class="bg-light p-2 rounded small">{{ modele() | json }}</pre>
      @if (envoye(); as texte) {
        <h2 class="h6">Dernier envoi</h2>
        <pre class="bg-success-subtle p-2 rounded small">{{ texte }}</pre>
      }
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
  • line 6: [(ngSubmit)]: with [FormsModule], the form is never submitted by the browser (no page reload); the [envoyer] method is called instead. [preventDefault()] is no longer needed (see Example 04);
  • lines 12–13: radio buttons: the same [ngModel] on each button, and one value per button ([[value]]). The signal receives the value of the selected button;
  • line 21: [[(ngModel)]="nom"] binds the field to the signal [nom], in both directions. The syntax [[( )]], known as a “banana in a box,” combines a property binding [[ngModel]] (from the signal to the field) and an event binding [(ngModelChange)] (from the field to the signal). In a [<form>], each field linked by [ngModel] must have a [name] attribute;
  • line 26: with [type="number"], the signal receives a number;
  • line 33: [[ngModelOptions]="{ updateOn: 'blur' }"]: the signal is updated only when the field is exited, not with each keystroke;
  • line 37: a single field: [true] / [false];
  • lines 45–46: the leisure fields, managed manually: [[checked]] and [(change)], as in example 04;
  • lines 54–59: a drop-down list: the signal receives the value ([[value]], the country code) of the selected option;
  • line 63: a multiple-choice list ([multiple]): the signal receives the list of selected values;
  • line 72: a date: the signal receives a string ["yyyy-MM-dd"];
  • line 79: [{{ modele() | json }}]: the template, in JSON format, in real time;
  • line 80: [@if (envoye(); as texte)]: if the value is “true” (in this case, a non-empty string), the block is displayed, and [as texte] makes it a variable of the block.

[npm start 05-ngmodel]; fill out the form, then submit it:

[ngModel] has existed since the first version of [Angular] and accepts signals from [Angular] 17. It is found in countless applications. However, it leaves it up to the component to handle anything beyond the simple back-and-forth of a value: merging fields, determining which ones have been modified, validating them... The following example shows the most recent way to write a form.

docs.title: 2.6. Example 06: Signal-Based Forms
docs.text:
[Angular] 22 introduces a new way to write forms, entirely based on signals: signal-based forms ([Signal Forms], package [@angular/forms/signals]). The principle:

  • the form template is the UN signal, which contains an object with one property per field;
  • the function [form(modele)] constructs a field tree ([FieldTree]) that has the same structure as the template: [f.nom], [f.age], [f.newsletter]...;
  • In the template, [[formField]="f.nom"] links a field (HTML) to a field in the tree.

The form reads from and writes to the model; and each field knows its status: has it been accessed, modified, is it disabled, or is it valid?

// =========================================================================
// 06-signal-forms/src/app/app.ts - signal forms
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The modern way (Angular 22) to write a form:
//    1. MODÈLE: a signal that contains an object, with one property per
//       field (the form reads from and writes to this signal);
//    2. form(model, schema): creates a ARBRE DE CHAMPS (FieldTree), which
//       has the same form as the template: f.nom, f.age, f.newsletter... The
//       schema (optional) describes the field rules (see example 07);
//    3. [formField]="f.nom" links a HTML field to a field in the tree.
// Each field has a ÉTAT, obtained by calling it: f.nom() returns its value
// (value()), if it has been touched (touched()), modified (dirty()), or if it is
// disabled (disabled())...
// =========================================================================

import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { JsonPipe } from '@angular/common';
import { disabled, form, FormField } from '@angular/forms/signals';

// the format of the form data
interface Profil {
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
  age: number;
  newsletter: boolean;
  email: string;
  pays: string;
  naissance: string;
  presentation: string;
}

const DEPART: Profil = {
  titre: 'Mme',
  prenom: 'Marie',
  nom: 'PELISSIER',
  age: 30,
  newsletter: false,
  email: '',
  pays: 'fr',
  naissance: '',
  presentation: '',
};

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  imports: [FormField, JsonPipe],
  templateUrl: './app.html',
})
export class App {
  protected readonly titres = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];

   // 1. the template
  protected readonly modele = signal<Profil>({ ...DEPART });

   // 2. the field tree; a rule: the email address can only be edited if the
   // "newsletter" checkbox is selected (valueOf reads the value of a AUTRE field)
  protected readonly f = form(this.modele, (p) => {
    disabled(p.email, ({ valueOf }) => !valueOf(p.newsletter));
  });

   // the fields whose status is displayed in the table on the right
  protected readonly champs = ['prenom', 'nom', 'age', 'email'] as const;

  protected reinitialiser(): void {
     // reset the template to its default value and clear the fields
    this.modele.set({ ...DEPART });
    this.f().reset();
  }

  protected majuscules(): void {
     // Modify MODÈLE with the code: the fields follow
    this.modele.update((m) => ({ ...m, nom: m.nom.toUpperCase(), prenom: m.prenom.toUpperCase() }));
  }
}
  • line 18: the functions and directive for signal-based forms;
  • lines 21–31: the format of the form data;
  • line 47: the component imports the [FormField] directive, which is that of [[formField]];
  • line 54: the template—a signal containing a [Profil] object;
  • lines 58–60: the field tree. The second argument of [form] is the form schema: a function that receives the field paths ([p.email], [p.newsletter]...) and attaches rules to them. Here, there is only one: [disabled(p.email, logique)] disables the field [email] when the function [logique] returns [true]. [valueOf(p.newsletter)] reads the value of another field: the email address can only be edited if the “newsletter” checkbox is selected. The rule is reactive: it is re-evaluated as soon as the checkbox changes. Example 07 will add validation rules;
  • line 63: the names of the fields whose status is displayed by the template; [as const] creates a list of exact names (['prenom' | 'nom' | ...]), not arbitrary strings;
  • lines 65–69: the reset. The template is reset to its initial value (the fields follow), then the field states are reset to zero ([touched], [dirty]): [f()] (the tree, called) returns the state of the entire form, including the [reset()] method;
  • Lines 71–74: Modify the template with the code; the page fields follow.

The template:

<div class="container py-4">
  <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 06 - les formulaires à signaux</h1>
  <div class="row g-4">
    <form class="col-md-7" (submit)="$event.preventDefault()">
      <div class="mb-3">
        <span class="form-label d-block">Titre</span>
         <!-- radio buttons: the same field, one value per button -->
        @for (t of titres; track t) {
          <div class="form-check form-check-inline">
            <input type="radio" class="form-check-input" [id]="'titre-' + t" [value]="t" [formField]="f.titre">
            <label class="form-check-label" [for]="'titre-' + t">{{ t }}</label>
          </div>
        }
      </div>
      <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
        <div class="col-5">
          <label class="form-label" for="prenom">Prénom</label>
           <!-- [formField]: this field (HTML) edits the field f.prenom in the form -->
          <input id="prenom" class="form-control" [formField]="f.prenom">
        </div>
        <div class="col-5">
          <label class="form-label" for="nom">Nom</label>
          <input id="nom" class="form-control" [formField]="f.nom">
        </div>
        <div class="col-2">
          <label class="form-label" for="age">Âge</label>
           <!-- type="number" and a "number" type template: a numeric value -->
          <input id="age" type="number" class="form-control" [formField]="f.age">
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="row g-3 mb-3 align-items-end">
        <div class="col-5">
          <div class="form-check">
            <input id="newsletter" type="checkbox" class="form-check-input" [formField]="f.newsletter">
            <label for="newsletter" class="form-check-label">Recevoir la lettre d'information</label>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="col-7">
          <label class="form-label" for="email">E-mail (si lettre d'information)</label>
           <!-- "disabled" is managed by the form: no attribute to specify here -->
          <input id="email" type="email" class="form-control" [formField]="f.email">
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="row g-3 mb-3">
        <div class="col-6">
          <label class="form-label" for="pays">Pays</label>
          <select id="pays" class="form-select" [formField]="f.pays">
            <option value="fr">France</option>
            <option value="be">Belgique</option>
            <option value="ch">Suisse</option>
          </select>
        </div>
        <div class="col-6">
          <label class="form-label" for="naissance">Date de naissance</label>
          <input id="naissance" type="date" class="form-control" [formField]="f.naissance">
        </div>
      </div>
      <div class="mb-3">
        <label class="form-label" for="presentation">Présentation</label>
        <textarea id="presentation" rows="2" class="form-control" [formField]="f.presentation"></textarea>
      </div>
      <div class="d-flex gap-2">
        <button type="button" class="btn btn-outline-primary" (click)="majuscules()">Nom en majuscules</button>
        <button type="button" class="btn btn-outline-secondary" (click)="reinitialiser()">Réinitialiser</button>
      </div>
    </form>

    <div class="col-md-5">
      <h2 class="h6">Le modèle, en direct</h2>
       <!-- f().value(): the value of the entire form, i.e., the model -->
      <pre class="bg-light p-2 rounded small">{{ f().value() | json }}</pre>
      <h2 class="h6">L'état des champs</h2>
      <table class="table table-sm small">
        <thead><tr><th>champ</th><th>touched</th><th>dirty</th><th>disabled</th></tr></thead>
        <tbody>
          @for (c of champs; track c) {
            <tr>
              <td>{{ c }}</td>
              <td>{{ f[c]().touched() }}</td>
              <td>{{ f[c]().dirty() }}</td>
              <td>{{ f[c]().disabled() }}</td>
            </tr>
          }
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <p class="small mb-0">formulaire modifié (dirty) : <strong>{{ f().dirty() }}</strong></p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
  • line 4: the form is not submitted (no submit button in this example); we only prevent submission via the Enter key;
  • line 10: radio buttons: the same field [f.titre] on each button, one value per button;
  • line 19: [[formField]="f.prenom"] links the field HTML to the field [prenom] in the form, in both directions, as with [ngModel] in example 05;
  • line 28: a numeric field, for a numeric property of the model: the model receives a number;
  • line 34: a checkbox, for a Boolean value;
  • line 41: the field [email]. Do not specify the attribute [disabled]: the directive [[formField]] sets and removes it automatically, according to the schema rule;
  • lines 47, 55, 60: a drop-down list, a date, a text box;
  • Line 71: [f().value()]: the value of the entire form, i.e., the template;
  • Lines 76–83: the status of four fields. [f[c]] is the field with the name [c]; [fc] is its status; [touched()] (the user entered the field and then exited it), [dirty()] (the user changed its value), [disabled()]: all signals;
  • Line 86: the status of the entire form—it is updated if any of its fields are modified.

[npm start 06-formulaires-signaux]; select the title, enter a first name, last name, and age, check the box (the email field becomes editable), enter the email address, then click “Capitalize Name”:

Compared to [ngModel]: a single signal for the entire form, and the status of each field, without having to write anything. Signal-based forms cannot link multiple checkboxes to the same list, nor can they link to a multiple-choice list: for these fields, use the technique from Example 05.

docs.title: 2.7. Example 07: Form Validation
docs.text:
The “Create an Account” form from the [RdvMedecins] application, validated in the browser using the same rules as the server: title in the list, first and last name required (20 characters maximum), username in lowercase, password at least 6 characters long, confirmation.

Note: This validation is merely for the user’s convenience (an immediate response, without back-and-forth communication with the server). It provides no security: anyone can send a manually crafted request to the server ([curl]...). The server will therefore validate “TOUJOURS” as well (see Example 25).

docs.title: 2.7.1. Application configuration
docs.text:
import { bootstrapApplication } from '@angular/platform-browser';
import { provideSignalFormsConfig } from '@angular/forms/signals';
import { App } from './app/app';

bootstrapApplication(App, {
  providers: [
    provideSignalFormsConfig({
      classes: {
         // A field with an error is only flagged once it has been "touched" (exited)
        'is-invalid': (champ) => champ.state().touched() && champ.state().invalid(),
        'is-valid': (champ) => champ.state().touched() && champ.state().valid(),
      },
    }),
  ],
}).catch((erreur) => console.error(erreur));
  • line 15: the second argument of [bootstrapApplication] is the application configuration: a list of providers ([providers]), which make services and settings available to the entire application (see Example 14);
  • Lines 17–23: [provideSignalFormsConfig] configures the signal-based forms. [classes] associates a class CSS with a condition based on the state of a field: the directive [[formField]] applies the class to the field HTML when the condition is true. The following classes from [Bootstrap] are used:
    • line 20: [is-invalid] (red border), if the field has been entered but is invalid (ET). Errors are not displayed immediately: an empty form covered in red is unappealing;
    • line 21: [is-valid] (green box), if the field has been entered and is valid.

docs.title: 2.7.2. The component
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 07-validation/src/app/app.ts - validate a form in the browser
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Field rules are defined in the form’s SCHÉMA (second
// form argument): required, maxLength, minLength, pattern... and
// validate() for a "custom" rule. Each field then knows its
// errors (f.nom().errors()), recalculated with every keystroke.
// We don’t display them right away (an empty form covered in red is
//(unpleasant): only for a field that has already been exited ("touched"). submit()
// marks all fields as touched, then executes the action only if the
// form is valid.
//
// Same rules as the RdvMedecins server (“Create an Account” form).
// ATTENTION: This validation is simply a CONFORT for the user (an
// an immediate response, without any back-and-forth with the server). It does not protect
// anything: anyone can send the server a request fabricated by
// (curl...). The server therefore revalidates TOUJOURS everything (see Example 25).
// =========================================================================

import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { form, FormField, maxLength, minLength, pattern, required, submit, validate } from '@angular/forms/signals';

interface Compte {
  titre: string;
  prenom: string;
  nom: string;
  login: string;
  password: string;
  confirmation: string;
}

const TITRES = ['Mr', 'Mme', 'Melle'];
const FORMAT_LOGIN = /^[a-z0-9._-]{1,30}$/;
const MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN = 6;

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  imports: [FormField],
  templateUrl: './app.html',
})
export class App {
  protected readonly titres = TITRES;
  protected readonly modele = signal<Compte>({
    titre: 'Mr',
    prenom: '',
    nom: '',
    login: '',
    password: '',
    confirmation: '',
  });

   // the schema: p denotes the CHEMINS of the fields (p.nom, p.login...)
  protected readonly f = form(this.modele, (p) => {
    validate(p.titre, ({ value }) =>
      TITRES.includes(value()) ? null : { kind: 'titre', message: 'Choisissez un titre dans la liste.' },
    );
    required(p.prenom, { message: 'Le prénom est obligatoire.' });
    maxLength(p.prenom, 20, { message: 'Le prénom ne doit pas dépasser 20 caractères.' });
    required(p.nom, { message: 'Le nom est obligatoire.' });
    maxLength(p.nom, 20, { message: 'Le nom ne doit pas dépasser 20 caractères.' });
    required(p.login, { message: 'Le login est obligatoire.' });
    pattern(p.login, FORMAT_LOGIN, { message: 'Lettres minuscules non accentuées, chiffres, point, tiret, souligné.' });
    required(p.password, { message: 'Le mot de passe est obligatoire.' });
    minLength(p.password, MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN, { message: `Au moins ${MOT_DE_PASSE_MIN} caractères.` });
     // a "custom" rule that compares DEUX fields (valueOf reads the other)
    validate(p.confirmation, ({ value, valueOf }) =>
      value() === valueOf(p.password)
        ? null
        : { kind: 'confirmation', message: 'La confirmation ne correspond pas au mot de passe.' },
    );
  });

  protected readonly envoiTente = signal(false);
  protected readonly succes = signal(false);

   // (submit) the form
  protected async envoyer(evenement: SubmitEvent): Promise<void> {
    evenement.preventDefault();
    this.envoiTente.set(true);
     // submit() marks all fields as touched (their errors
     // are displayed), then executes the action only if everything is valid
    const valide = await submit(this.f, async () => {
       // here, we would send the form to the server (see Example 25)
      return null; // null: no errors
    });
    this.succes.set(valide);
  }
}
  • line 21: validation functions for forms with indicators;
  • lines 53–71: the form schema: each function associates a rule with a field, identified by its path ([p.prenom]), along with the message to display in case of failure:
    • [required]: the field must be filled in;
    • [maxLength], [minLength]: a maximum or minimum length;
    • [pattern]: the value must match a regular expression;
    • [validate(chemin, fonction)]: a “custom” rule. The function receives the field’s context (its value [value()], the value of another field [valueOf(...)]) and returns [null] (no error) or an error: an object [{ kind, message }], where [kind] indicates the error type (lines 54–56 and 66–70). The confirmation rule compares two fields: it is re-evaluated when one (OU) changes and the other does not;
    • [Angular] also provides [email], [min], [max], and asynchronous rules ([validateHttp]), which query a server;
  • lines 77–87: sending. [submit(formulaire, action)]:
    • marks all fields as affected: their errors appear, even for those the user has never visited;
    • Executes the action only if the form is valid;
    • returns [true] if the submission was successful. The action returns [null] when everything goes well, or error codes, which Example 25 will retrieve from the server.
