docs.title: 3.3. Example 12: Content Projection
docs.text: Inputs transmit data; content projection transmits content (from HTML and other components), written by the parent ENTRE into the component’s tags. This is the client-side equivalent of the [layout.hbs] template for the [NestJS] course and its [{{{body}}}].

docs.title: 3.3.1. A card
docs.text:
A reusable frame (border, header, footer), whose parent provides the content:

// =========================================================================
// 12-projection/src/app/carte/carte.ts - a reusable GABARIT
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The entries transmit DONNÉES; the content PROJECTION transmits
// from CONTENU (from HTML, other components), written by the parent ENTRE the
// <app-map> and </app-map> tags. The map defines the frame (border,
// header, footer), while the parent element provides the content inside:
//    - <ng-content /                  > : the “main” content;
//    - <ng-content select="[entete]" />: only elements that have
//                                         the header attribute;
//    - the content placed between <ng-content> and </ng-content> is displayed if
//      the parent provides nothing (default content).
// This is the client-side equivalent of the template layout.hbs and its {{{body}}}
// in the course NestJS.
// =========================================================================

import { Component, input } from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-carte',
  template: `
    <div class="card mb-3" [class]="couleur() ? 'border-' + couleur() : ''">
      <div class="card-header" [class]="couleur() ? 'text-bg-' + couleur() : ''">
        <ng-content select="[entete]">Sans titre</ng-content>
      </div>
      <div class="card-body">
        <ng-content />
      </div>
       <!-- An empty footer (the parent provided nothing) is hidden by the CSS :empty -->
      <div class="card-footer text-muted small"><ng-content select="[pied]" /></div>
    </div>
  `,
  styles: `
    .card-footer:empty {
      display: none;
    }
  `,
})
export class Carte {
  readonly couleur = input<'primary' | 'success' | 'danger'>();
}
  • line 27: [<ng-content />]: the location where [Angular] places the content written by the parent between [<app-carte>] and [</app-carte>];
  • line 24: [<ng-content select="[entete]">]: only those content elements that have the [entete] attribute. [select] accepts a CSS selector (a tag, a class, or an attribute). The text between [<ng-content>] and [</ng-content>] is displayed if the parent element does not provide any content: this is the default content;
  • line 30: the footer: elements that have the [pied] attribute;
  • lines 33–37: an empty footer (the parent element provided nothing) is hidden: the pseudo-class CSS [:empty] denotes an element with no content;
  • Line 40: An optional entry that can take only three values; if no default value is specified, it defaults to [undefined].

docs.title: 3.3.2. A generic array
docs.text:
An array that knows how to iterate through rows but doesn’t know how to display UNE per row: its parent tells it how by passing it a row template.

// =========================================================================
// 12-projection/src/app/tableau/tableau.ts - an array GÉNÉRIQUE
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Array<T> is a generic class: it displays rows of any
// type T. It knows how to iterate over the rows, but not how to display UNE
// row: the parent tells it how, by passing it a MODÈLE row
// (an <ng-template #line>, a piece of HTML that isn’t displayed as
// as that, but which can be displayed on demand, as many times as needed).
//
// contentChild('row'): the <ng-template #row> placed by the parent between
// <app-table> and </app-table>. The table displays it for each row
// with ngTemplateOutlet, passing it a CONTEXTE: the row ($implicit)
// and its rank (index). The content provided by the parent therefore uses
// data that belongs to the child.
// =========================================================================

import { Component, contentChild, input, TemplateRef } from '@angular/core';
import { NgTemplateOutlet } from '@angular/common';

// what the array passes to the model for each row
export interface ContexteLigne<T> {
  $implicit: T; // the value retrieved by let-row
  index: number; // retrieved by let-i="index"
}

@Component({
  selector: 'app-tableau',
  imports: [NgTemplateOutlet],
  template: `
    <table class="table table-sm align-middle mb-0">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          @for (c of colonnes(); track c) {
            <th>{{ c }}</th>
          }
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        @for (l of lignes(); track l.id; let i = $index) {
          <tr>
            <ng-container [ngTemplateOutlet]="modeleLigne() ?? null" [ngTemplateOutletContext]="{ $implicit: l, index: i }" />
          </tr>
        } @empty {
          <tr>
            <td class="text-muted" [attr.colspan]="colonnes().length">
              <ng-content select="[vide]">Aucune donnée.</ng-content>
            </td>
          </tr>
        }
      </tbody>
    </table>
  `,
})
export class Tableau<T extends { id: number }> {
  readonly lignes = input.required<T[]>();
  readonly colonnes = input.required<string[]>();
  protected readonly modeleLigne = contentChild<TemplateRef<ContexteLigne<T>>>('ligne');
}
  • line 54: [Tableau<T>] is a generic class: it displays lines of any type [T], provided they have a [id] (for [track], line 39);
  • Line 57: [contentChild('ligne')]: a signal that refers to the element of the projected content marked [#ligne]. This will be a [<ng-template>]: a portion of HTML that is not displayed as-is, but can be displayed on demand, as many times as necessary (a [TemplateRef]);
  • line 41: the [ngTemplateOutlet] directive displays a template by passing it a context—an object whose properties become variables in the template. [$implicit] is the default value (lines 21–24);
  • lines 43–49: if the list is empty, the block [@empty], with projected content ([[vide]]) and default content;
  • line 45: [[attr.colspan]]: an attribute binding, since [colspan] is not a property of the [<td>] element.

docs.title: 3.3.3. The parent
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 12-projection/src/app/app.ts - use the Map and Table templates
// =========================================================================

import { Component, computed, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { Carte } from './carte/carte';
import { Tableau } from './tableau/tableau';

interface Creneau {
  id: number;
  horaire: string;
  patient: string | null;
}

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  imports: [Carte, Tableau],
  templateUrl: './app.html',
})
export class App {
  protected readonly creneaux = signal<Creneau[]>([
    { id: 1, horaire: '8:00 - 8:20', patient: null },
    { id: 2, horaire: '8:20 - 8:40', patient: 'Mme Alice DURAND' },
    { id: 3, horaire: '8:40 - 9:00', patient: null },
  ]);
  protected readonly libres = computed(() => this.creneaux().filter((c) => c.patient === null).length);
  protected readonly personne: { id: number; nom: string }[] = [];
}

<div class="container py-4" style="max-width: 720px">
  <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 12 - la projection de contenu</h1>

  <app-carte couleur="primary">
     <!-- the header attribute: this <span> will go inside the <ng-content select="[entete]"> -->
    <span entete>Agenda de Mme PELISSIER</span>
     <!-- Everything that has neither a header nor a footer goes into the main <ng-content /> -->
    <app-tableau [lignes]="creneaux()" [colonnes]="['#', 'Créneau', 'Statut']">
       <!-- The template for a row: let-c holds the row, let-i its index -->
      <ng-template #line let-c let-i="index">
        <td>{{ i + 1 }}</td>
        <td>{{ c.horaire }}</td>
        <td>
          @if (c.patient) {
            <span class="badge text-bg-secondary">{{ c.patient }}</span>
          } @else {
            <span class="badge text-bg-success">Libre</span>
          }
        </td>
      </ng-template>
    </app-tableau>
    <span pied>{{ libres() }} créneau(x) libre(s)</span>
  </app-carte>

  <app-carte couleur="success">
    <span entete>Une carte sans pied</span>
    <p class="mb-0">Le pied n'est pas fourni : la carte ne l'affiche pas.</p>
  </app-carte>

  <app-carte>
     <!-- No header provided: the default content, “Untitled” -->
    <app-tableau [lignes]="personne" [colonnes]="['Nom']">
      <span vide>Personne pour l'instant.</span>
    </app-tableau>
  </app-carte>
</div>
  • lines 4–23: a blueprint. Its content is distributed by the blueprint: [<span entete>] (line 6) goes into the header, [<span pied>] (line 22) into the footer, and the rest (the table) into the body;
  • lines 10–20: the template for a line. [let-c] retrieves the value [$implicit] from the context (the line), and [let-i="index"] retrieves its property [index]. The content provided by the parent thus uses data that belongs to the child;
  • lines 25–28: a card without a footer;
  • lines 30–35: a card without a footer (the default content, “Untitled”), and an empty table.

[npm start 12-projection]:

The compiler does not recognize the type of [c] in the template (lines 10–20): it treats it as [any]. This can be remedied (with a directive declaring the context type), at the cost of a little more code; this is the limitation of this technique.

docs.title: 3.4. Example 13: The Lifecycle of a Component
docs.text: A component is created, displayed, exists, and then disappears. [Angular] allows you to take action at each stage: this is the component’s lifecycle.

docs.title: 3.4.1. A clock
docs.text:
A clock starts a timer when it is created... and must stop it when it disappears: otherwise, the timer would continue to run for no reason (memory leak).

// =========================================================================
// 13-lifecycle/src/app/clock/horloge.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The lifecycle of a component:
//    1. constructo     r : the class is created; the inputs are not
//                          yet available;
//    2. ngOnIni        t : the inputs have been assigned their first values;
//    3. afterNextRende r : the component is AFFICHÉ; its elements HTML
//                          exist on the page;
//    4. ngOnDestro     y : the component will be RETIRÉ on the page.
// A clock starts a timer (setInterval) on startup... and must
// must stop it when it disappears: otherwise, the timer
// would continue to run for no reason (memory leak).
// =========================================================================

import { afterNextRender, Component, OnDestroy, OnInit, output, signal } from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-horloge',
  template: `<div class="display-6 font-monospace">{{ heure() }}</div>`,
})
// implements OnInit, OnDestroy: TypeScript checks that the methods exist
export class Horloge implements OnInit, OnDestroy {
  readonly journal = output<string>();
  protected readonly heure = signal(new Date().toLocaleTimeString());
  private minuterie: number | undefined;

  constructor() {
    console.log('Horloge : constructor'); // the parent is not yet listening to the log
     // afterNextRender registers itself in the constructor; the function is
     // called once, immediately after the component is first displayed
    afterNextRender(() => this.journal.emit('Horloge : afterNextRender - affichée'));
  }

  ngOnInit(): void {
    this.journal.emit('Horloge : ngOnInit - démarrage de la minuterie');
    this.minuterie = window.setInterval(() => this.heure.set(new Date().toLocaleTimeString()), 1000);
  }

  ngOnDestroy(): void {
    window.clearInterval(this.minuterie);
    this.journal.emit('Horloge : ngOnDestroy - minuterie arrêtée');
  }
}

The steps:

  • lines 28–33: the constructor: the class is created. The inputs have not yet been assigned values, and the parent is not yet listening to the outputs (hence the [console.log] on line 29, rather than a [emit]);
  • lines 35–38: [ngOnInit()]: The inputs have received their first values. This is the usual place to trigger actions that depend on them: a load, a timer;
  • line 32: [afterNextRender(fonction)], called in the constructor, records a function executed once, immediately after the component is first displayed: its elements HTML then exist on the page;
  • Lines 40–43: [ngOnDestroy()]: the component is about to be removed from the page. The timer is stopped.

[implements OnInit, OnDestroy] (line 23) is not required: [Angular] calls [ngOnInit] if it exists. But [TypeScript] then verifies that the methods are written correctly.

[Angular] offers additional steps, which are less useful since the signals were introduced: [ngOnChanges] (an input has changed; we prefer a [computed] or a [effect] for that input), [ngAfterViewInit]... And an alternative to [ngOnDestroy]: [inject(DestroyRef).onDestroy(fonction)], which Example 14 will use.

docs.title: 3.4.2. The parent
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 13-lifecycle/src/app/app.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
//    - @if around <app-clock>: checking/unchecking the box creates/destroy
//      the component (ngOnInit / ngOnDestroy, see horloge.ts);
//    - viewChild('field'): a signal that returns the HTML element marked #field
//      in the template (undefined until it is displayed);
//    - effect: executed once, then whenever the
//      signals it reads. Here, to give focus to the field as soon as it
//      appears, and so that the tab title updates as the user types.
// =========================================================================

import { Component, effect, ElementRef, OnInit, signal, viewChild } from '@angular/core';
import { FormsModule } from '@angular/forms';
import { Horloge } from './horloge/horloge';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  imports: [FormsModule, Horloge],
  templateUrl: './app.html',
})
export class App implements OnInit {
  protected readonly avecHorloge = signal(true);
  protected readonly journal = signal<string[]>([]);
  protected readonly recherche = signal('');
  protected readonly afficherRecherche = signal(false);

   // the <input #field> element in the template; ElementRef.nativeElement: the HTML
  private readonly champ = viewChild<ElementRef<HTMLInputElement>>('champ');

  constructor() {
     // the field appears (viewChild changes): focus is given to it
    effect(() => this.champ()?.nativeElement.focus());
     // the tab title updates as you type, starting from the beginning
    effect(() => {
      const texte = this.recherche();
      document.title = texte ? `Recherche : ${texte}` : 'Exemple 13';
    });
  }

  ngOnInit(): void {
    this.tracer('App : ngOnInit');
  }

  protected tracer(message: string): void {
    this.journal.update((j) => [...j, `${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()} ${message}`]);
  }
}
  • line 29: [viewChild('champ')]: a signal that refers to the template element marked [#champ]. It is set to [undefined] as long as the element does not exist (the field appears only after a click). [ElementRef] wraps the element HTML, which is accessible via its property [nativeElement];
  • line 33: a [effect] that reads this signal: when the field appears, the effect is triggered again and gives it focus. There is no need to “wait” for the page to refresh: the signal only changes once the element has been created;
  • lines 35–38: a second effect: the tab title updates as text is entered, starting from the very beginning (an effect always runs once at the start);
  • lines 41–43: the parent element also has its own [ngOnInit].
<div class="container py-4" style="max-width: 720px">
  <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 13 - le cycle de vie d'un composant</h1>

  <div class="card p-3 mb-3">
    <label class="form-check-label mb-2">
      <input type="checkbox" class="form-check-input" [(ngModel)]="avecHorloge"> afficher l'horloge
    </label>
    @if (avecHorloge()) {
      <app-horloge (journal)="tracer($event)" />
    }
  </div>

  <div class="card p-3 mb-3">
    @if (!afficherRecherche()) {
      <button class="btn btn-outline-primary align-self-start" (click)="afficherRecherche.set(true)">Rechercher...</button>
    } @else {
       <!-- #field: the element referred to by viewChild('field') -->
      <input #field class="form-control" placeholder="the tab title follows the input" [(ngModel)]="search">
    }
  </div>

  <h2 class="h6">Journal</h2>
  <ol class="small">
    @for (ligne of journal(); track $index) {
      <li>{{ ligne }}</li>
    }
  </ol>
</div>
  • lines 8–10: Checking or unchecking the box creates or destroys the clock: [@if] actually adds or removes the component from the page;
  • line 18: [#champ], the element referred to by [viewChild('champ')].

[npm start 13-cycle-de-vie]; uncheck and then recheck the box, and click “Search...”:

The log shows the order of the steps: first the parent ([App : ngOnInit]), then the clock ([ngOnInit], [afterNextRender]), its destruction ([ngOnDestroy]), and a new clock. The search field has focus.

docs.title: 3.5. Example 14: Services and Dependency Injection
docs.text:
A service is a class that groups together data and code shared by multiple components: server access, the logged-in user, a shopping cart, etc. Components do not create services (never [new PanierService()]): they request them from [Angular], using the [inject()] function. This is dependency injection, the mechanism that the [NestJS] course presented on the server side.

When a component requests a service, [Angular] looks for who provides it: the component itself, then its parent, the parent of its parent… all the way up to the application. Depending on where it is provided, a service is therefore shared to a greater or lesser extent. This example shows three levels.

docs.title: 3.5.1. A root service
docs.text:
import { Injectable, signal } from '@angular/core';

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class JournalService {
  private readonly _lignes = signal<string[]>([]);
   // asReadonly(): the LISENT components are the rows; only the service modifies them
  readonly lignes = this._lignes.asReadonly();

  tracer(message: string): void {
    this._lignes.update((l) => [`${new Date().toLocaleTimeString()} ${message}`, ...l].slice(0, 6));
  }
}
  • line 14: [@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })]: the service is provided at the root of the application. [Angular] creates a single instance of UN the first time it is requested, and everyone who requests it receives that instance;
  • Lines 16–18: The data in the lines is private; [asReadonly()] provides a public, read-only version of it. The components read the lines; only the service modifies them (line 21). This is the standard organization for a service that maintains state.

docs.title: 3.5.2. A service provided by a component
docs.text:
import { computed, inject, Injectable, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { JournalService } from './journal.service';

export interface Article {
  libelle: string;
  prix: number;
}

@Injectable()
export class PanierService {
   // A service can itself request other services
  private readonly journal = inject(JournalService);

  private readonly _articles = signal<Article[]>([]);
  readonly articles = this._articles.asReadonly();
  readonly total = computed(() => this._articles().reduce((somme, a) => somme + a.prix, 0));

  ajouter(article: Article): void {
    this._articles.update((a) => [...a, article]);
    this.journal.tracer(`panier : + ${article.libelle}`);
  }

  retirer(index: number): void {
    this.journal.tracer(`panier : - ${this._articles()[index].libelle}`);
    this._articles.update((a) => a.filter((_, i) => i !== index));
  }
}
  • line 19: [@Injectable()] SANS [providedIn]: the service is not provided by default anywhere. A component will provide it in its array [providers];
  • line 22: a service can itself request other services: the shopping cart is logged;
  • lines 24–26: the shopping cart's status (private), its read-only version, and its total;
  • lines 28–36: the two actions that change the status.

docs.title: 3.5.3. A configured service
docs.text:
import { DestroyRef, inject, Injectable, InjectionToken, signal } from '@angular/core';

// factory: the value used if no one provides this token
export const PERIODE_HORLOGE = new InjectionToken<number>('periode de l\'horloge', { factory: () => 1000 });

@Injectable()
export class HorlogeService {
  private readonly periode = inject(PERIODE_HORLOGE);
  readonly maintenant = signal(new Date());

  constructor() {
    const minuterie = window.setInterval(() => this.maintenant.set(new Date()), this.periode);
    inject(DestroyRef).onDestroy(() => window.clearInterval(minuterie));
  }
}
  • line 15: an injection token ([InjectionToken]) refers to a value that is not a class: in this case, a number—the clock period. [factory] provides the value used if no one supplies this token;
  • line 19: the token value is requested in the same way a service is requested;
  • line 24: [DestroyRef] represents the “lifetime” of the component that provided the service; [onDestroy] registers a function to be executed when it is destroyed: the timer stops along with the component that provided the clock.

[inject()] is called only in an injection context: when initializing the properties of a class created by [Angular] (component, service, directive, pipe), or in its constructor. It cannot be called later, within an ordinary method.

docs.title: 3.5.4. Components
docs.text:
A catalog that adds items to the shopping cart:

// 14-services/src/app/catalog/catalogue.ts - a descendant that INJECTE the shopping cart
import { Component, inject } from '@angular/core';
import { Article, PanierService } from '../services/panier.service';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-catalogue',
  template: `
    <ul class="list-group">
      @for (a of catalogue; track a.libelle) {
        <li class="list-group-item d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center">
          {{ a.libelle }} ({{ a.prix }} €)
          <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary" (click)="panier.ajouter(a)">Ajouter</button>
        </li>
      }
    </ul>
  `,
})
export class Catalogue {
   // the shopping cart provided by the app (runtime error if no one provides it)
  protected readonly panier = inject(PanierService);

  protected readonly catalogue: Article[] = [
    { libelle: 'Consultation', prix: 30 },
    { libelle: 'Vaccin', prix: 12.5 },
    { libelle: 'Certificat', prix: 5 },
  ];
}
  • line 20: [inject(PanierService)]: the shopping cart provided by a parent ([App]). If no one provided it, [Angular] would report a runtime error;
  • Line 12: The template directly calls a method of the service.

A summary of the shopping cart:

import { Component, inject } from '@angular/core';
import { DatePipe } from '@angular/common';
import { PanierService } from '../services/panier.service';
import { HorlogeService, PERIODE_HORLOGE } from '../services/horloge.service';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-resume-panier',
  imports: [DatePipe],
   // a new instance of HorlogeService for the CE component, with a
   // different period: { provide: token, useValue: value }
  providers: [HorlogeService, { provide: PERIODE_HORLOGE, useValue: 5000 }],
  template: `
    <div class="card p-3">
      <h2 class="h6">Panier ({{ panier.articles().length }} article(s)) - {{ horloge.maintenant() | date: 'HH:mm:ss' }}</h2>
      <ul class="mb-2">
        @for (a of panier.articles(); track $index) {
          <li>{{ a.libelle }} <a href="#" (click)="$event.preventDefault(); panier.retirer($index)">retirer</a></li>
        }
      </ul>
      <strong>Total : {{ panier.total() }} €</strong>
    </div>
  `,
})
export class ResumePanier {
  protected readonly panier = inject(PanierService);
  protected readonly horloge = inject(HorlogeService);
}
  • line 18: the component provides its own clock (a new instance of [HorlogeService]) and another time period: [{ provide: jeton, useValue: valeur }];
  • Lines 32–33: The shopping cart is that of [App] (the same as the one in the catalog); the clock is its own.

And the root component:

import { Component, inject } from '@angular/core';
import { DatePipe } from '@angular/common';
import { Catalogue } from './catalogue/catalogue';
import { ResumePanier } from './resume-panier/resume-panier';
import { HorlogeService } from './services/horloge.service';
import { JournalService } from './services/journal.service';
import { PanierService } from './services/panier.service';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  imports: [DatePipe, Catalogue, ResumePanier],
  providers: [PanierService, HorlogeService],
  templateUrl: './app.html',
})
export class App {
  protected readonly horloge = inject(HorlogeService);
  protected readonly journal = inject(JournalService);
}
  • line 23: [App] provides a basket (shared by it and all its descendants) and a clock (default period: one second);
  • line 28: the log, root service.
<div class="container py-4" style="max-width: 720px">
  <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 14 - les services et l'injection de dépendances</h1>
  <p class="text-muted">Horloge de App : {{ horloge.maintenant() | date: 'HH:mm:ss' }}</p>
  <div class="row g-3">
    <div class="col-md-6"><app-catalogue /></div>
    <div class="col-md-6"><app-resume-panier /></div>
  </div>
  <h2 class="h6 mt-3">Journal (JournalService)</h2>
  <ul class="small">
    @for (ligne of journal.lignes(); track $index) {
      <li>{{ ligne }}</li>
    }
  </ul>
</div>

[npm start 14-services]; three items are added, one is removed:

The two timers do not advance at the same rate: each component has received the instance closest to it. The shopping cart, meanwhile, is shared by both the catalog and the summary.

Services are the means, in [Angular], of sharing logic and data between components (the role played by “composables” and [provide] / [inject] in [Vue.js]). Example 20 will turn this into a state shared by the entire application.

docs.title: 3.6. Example 15: Writing Your Own Directives
docs.text: A component is a directive that has a template. A directive “on its own” does not have one: it attaches to an existing element (its host) to modify its appearance or behavior. [Angular] provides some ([ngModel], [routerLink], [ngTemplateOutlet]...); you can write your own. Here are three examples.

docs.title: 3.6.1. Highlight an element on hover
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 15-directives/src/app/directives/surligner.directive.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A DIRECTIVE from ATTRIBUT adds behavior to an existing element,
// without its own template: <li appSurligner="gold">. Its selector is an
// attribute selector (CSS).
// host: the bindings that the directive establishes on the element that contains it
// (its "host"):
//    - '[style.background-color]': a property of the element;
//    - '(mouseenter)            ' : an event of the element.
// =========================================================================

import { Directive, input, signal } from '@angular/core';

@Directive({
  selector: '[appSurligner]',
  host: {
     '[style.background-color]': 'hover() ? color() : null',
     '[style.transition]': '"background-color 0.2s"',
     '(mouseenter)': 'survole.set(true)',
     '(mouseleave)': 'survole.set(false)',
  },
})
export class SurlignerDirective {
   // the input has the selector name: <li appSurligner="gold"> fills it in
  readonly couleur = input('#fff3cd', { alias: 'appSurligner', transform: (c: string) => c || '#fff3cd' });
  protected readonly survole = signal(false);
}
  • line 15: [@Directive] instead of [@Component]: no template;
  • line 16: the selector is an attribute selector CSS: the directive applies to any element that has the attribute [appSurligner];
  • lines 17–22: [host]: the bindings that the directive applies to its host, written as in a template:
    • line 18: a property binding: the host’s background color when the mouse hovers over it ([null]: no color);
    • lines 20–21: event bindings: mouse entry and exit;
  • Line 26: An entry named after the selector (option [alias]): [<li appSurligner="gold">] populates both the selector and the entry. The function [transform] replaces an empty string with the default color.

docs.title: 3.6.2. Set focus
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 15-directives/src/app/directives/autofocus.directive.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// <input appAutofocus>: The field receives focus as soon as it is displayed.
// inject(ElementRef) returns the host element HTML (nativeElement).
// (The HTML autofocus attribute only works when the page loads;
// in a single-page application, the fields appear later.)
// =========================================================================

import { afterNextRender, Directive, ElementRef, inject } from '@angular/core';

@Directive({ selector: '[appAutofocus]' })
export class AutofocusDirective {
  constructor() {
    const element = inject<ElementRef<HTMLElement>>(ElementRef).nativeElement;
    afterNextRender(() => element.focus());
  }
}
  • line 15: [inject(ElementRef)] specifies the host element;
  • line 16: focus is given to it as soon as it is displayed. The attribute HTML [autofocus] only works when the page loads; in a single-page application, the fields appear later.

docs.title: 3.6.3. A long click
docs.text:
A directive can also trigger events. This one triggers its event only if the host is held down for one second: a safeguard against accidental clicks.

// =========================================================================
// 15-directives/src/app/directives/clic-long.directive.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A directive can also ÉMETTRE events (output):
//      <button (appClicLong)="delete()">
// The event is triggered only if the button is held down for one second:
// protection against accidental clicks. While the button is pressed, the class
// CSS "pressed" is applied to the button.
// =========================================================================

import { DestroyRef, Directive, inject, input, output, signal } from '@angular/core';

@Directive({
  selector: '[appClicLong]',
  host: {
     '[class.appui]': 'enCours()',
     '(pointerdown)': 'start()',
     '(pointerup)': 'stop()',
     '(pointerleave)': 'stop()',
  },
})
export class ClicLongDirective {
  readonly duree = input(1000); // in milliseconds
  readonly appClicLong = output<void>();
  protected readonly enCours = signal(false);
  private minuterie: number | undefined;

  constructor() {
    inject(DestroyRef).onDestroy(() => window.clearTimeout(this.minuterie));
  }

  protected commencer(): void {
    this.enCours.set(true);
    this.minuterie = window.setTimeout(() => {
      this.enCours.set(false);
      this.appClicLong.emit();
    }, this.duree());
  }

  protected arreter(): void {
    window.clearTimeout(this.minuterie);
    this.enCours.set(false);
  }
}
  • line 16: while the host is pressed, the class [appui] is applied to the host;
  • lines 17–19: pointer events (mouse, finger, stylus): press, release, exit the element;
  • line 24: an output bearing the selector’s name: we write [(appClicLong)="..."], and apply the directive at the same time as we listen for its event;
  • line 29: the timer is stopped if the host disappears.

docs.title: 3.6.4. Usage
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 15-directives/src/app/app.ts - write your own directives
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A component is a directive AVEC a template. A "short" directive
// "short" directive has no template: it attaches to an existing element to
// modify its appearance or behavior. Like a component, it must
// be imported by the component that uses it.
// =========================================================================

import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { AutofocusDirective } from './directives/autofocus.directive';
import { ClicLongDirective } from './directives/clic-long.directive';
import { SurlignerDirective } from './directives/surligner.directive';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  imports: [AutofocusDirective, ClicLongDirective, SurlignerDirective],
  templateUrl: './app.html',
  styles: `
    .appui {
      outline: 4px solid #dc3545;
    }
  `,
})
export class App {
  protected readonly medecins = signal(['Mme Marie PELISSIER', 'Mr Paul TATOU', 'Melle Sophie DUPONT']);
  protected readonly message = signal('');

  protected supprimer(nom: string): void {
    this.medecins.update((m) => m.filter((x) => x !== nom));
    this.message.set(`${nom} a été supprimé.`);
  }
}
  • line 17: Like a component, a directive must be imported by the component that uses it;
  • lines 19–23: the style of the [appui] class, set by the long-click directive.
<div class="container py-4" style="max-width: 640px">
  <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 15 - écrire ses propres directives</h1>
   <!-- appAutofocus: the field has focus as soon as the page is displayed -->
  <input appAutofocus class="form-control mb-3" placeholder="ce champ a reçu le focus tout seul">

  <p class="small text-muted">Survolez les lignes ; maintenez un bouton enfoncé une seconde pour supprimer.</p>
  <ul class="list-group mb-3">
    @for (m of medecins(); track m; let pair = $even) {
       <!-- appSurligner: if left blank, the default color; if specified, the given color -->
      <li class="list-group-item d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center"
          [appSurligner]="pair ? '' : '#d1e7dd'">
        {{ m }}
        <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger" (appClicLong)="supprimer(m)">Supprimer (appui long)</button>
      </li>
    }
  </ul>
  @if (message()) {
    <p class="alert alert-info">{{ message() }}</p>
  }
</div>
  • Line 4: The field will have focus as soon as it is displayed;
  • line 8: [let pair = $even]: Is the row number even?
  • line 11: every other row is highlighted in the default color, the other in green;
  • Line 13: A long press removes the doctor.

[npm start 15-directives]; hold down the second button, then hover over the first row:

docs.title: 3.7. Example 16: A Reusable Confirmation Window
docs.text:
Before deleting an item, the user is asked to confirm. The browser provides [window.confirm()], but its window cannot be formatted or translated. This example replaces it with a [Bootstrap] window, combining what the previous examples have demonstrated: a service (Example 14) that carries the window’s state in a signal, and a component that displays it. The case study will use exactly this mechanism.

16-confirmation/src/app/
├── confirmation/
│   ├── confirmation.service.ts   le service : la question posée, la réponse
│   └── fenetre-confirmation.ts   la fenêtre modale
├── app.ts
└── app.html

docs.title: 3.7.1. The service
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 16-confirmation/src/app/confirmation/confirmation.service.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// “Are you sure?”: window.confirm() exists, but you can neither
// style it or translate its buttons. It is replaced by a window
// Bootstrap window (fenetre-confirmation.ts), controlled by this service.
//
// Tip: confirm(message) returns a PROMESSE, which resolves to true (Yes)
// or false (No) when the user responds. The calling code is written
// just as simply as with window.confirm:
//
//      if (await this.confirmation.confirmer('Delete this doctor?')) { ... }
//
// providedIn: 'root': a single service for the entire application, so a
// single window, created once in the root component.
// =========================================================================

import { Injectable, signal } from '@angular/core';

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class ConfirmationService {
  private readonly _message = signal<string | null>(null); // null: window closed
  readonly message = this._message.asReadonly();
  private repondre: ((oui: boolean) => void) | null = null;

  confirmer(texte: string): Promise<boolean> {
    this.repondre?.(false); // Is a question still open? It defaults to "no"
    this._message.set(texte);
    return new Promise<boolean>((resolve) => {
      this.repondre = resolve;
    });
  }

  reponse(oui: boolean): void {
    this._message.set(null);
    const r = this.repondre;
    this.repondre = null;
    r?.(oui);
  }
}
  • line 20: a single service for the entire application; therefore, there will be only one window, placed once and for all in the root component;
  • line 22: the displayed message; [null] means that the window is closed;
  • line 23: [asReadonly()]: components can read the message, but only the service can modify it;
  • line 24: the function that will resolve the current promise, which is awaiting a response;
  • lines 26–32: [confirmer] opens the window (line 28) and returns a promise. Its function [resolve] is set aside (line 30): the promise will not be resolved until later, when the user clicks a button;
  • line 27: if a question were still open, it would be answered “no”: its promise will not remain pending forever;
  • lines 34–39: [reponse] is called by the window: it closes the window (line 35) and then resolves the promise with the user’s response (line 38).

This is the benefit of the promise: the code that asks the question writes it as a call to [window.confirm()], waiting for the response with [await], without a callback function.

docs.title: 3.7.2. The window
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 16-confirmation/src/app/confirmation/fenetre-confirmation.ts
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The modal window, placed UNE times within the root component:
//    - same Bootstrap classes as a real modal (.modal, .modal-backdrop),
//      displayed "hard-coded" (show d-block): no need for the JavaScript from
//      Bootstrap;
//    - keyboard: Esc = No; focus is placed on the "No" button (the
//      least risky choice) upon opening.
// '(document:keydown.escape)' in host: an event is listened for on the
// DOCUMENT, not on the component element.
// =========================================================================

import { Component, effect, ElementRef, inject, viewChild } from '@angular/core';
import { ConfirmationService } from './confirmation.service';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-fenetre-confirmation',
  host: { '(document:keydown.escape)': 'confirmation.message() !== null && confirmation.reponse(false)' },
  template: `
    @if (confirmation.message(); as message) {
      <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
      <div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"
           (click)="$event.target === $event.currentTarget && confirmation.reponse(false)">
        <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
          <div class="modal-content">
            <div class="modal-header">
              <h5 class="modal-title">Confirmation</h5>
              <button type="button" class="btn-close" aria-label="Fermer" (click)="confirmation.reponse(false)"></button>
            </div>
            <div class="modal-body">
              <p class="mb-0">{{ message }}</p>
            </div>
            <div class="modal-footer">
              <button #boutonNon type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" (click)="confirmation.reponse(false)">No, go back</button>
              <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" (click)="confirmation.reponse(true)">Oui, confirmer</button>
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    }
  `,
})
export class FenetreConfirmation {
  protected readonly confirmation = inject(ConfirmationService);
  private readonly boutonNon = viewChild<ElementRef<HTMLButtonElement>>('boutonNon');

  constructor() {
     // Upon opening, the "No" button appears: it receives focus
    effect(() => this.boutonNon()?.nativeElement.focus());
  }
}
  • line 19: [document:keydown.escape]: the event is listened for on the entire document, not on the component’s element. The Esc key responds with “no” if a question is asked;
  • line 21: the window only appears if a message needs to be displayed; [as message] assigns a name to the signal’s value;
  • Lines 22–23: The classes of a true modal [Bootstrap], displayed directly ([show d-block]): The [JavaScript] derived from [Bootstrap] is unnecessary, since [Angular] determines the display;
  • line 24: a click next to the dialog box (on the gray background) responds with “no.” [$event.target === $event.currentTarget]: the click occurred on the [.modal] element itself, not on one of its children;
  • lines 35–36: both responses. The “No” button carries the template variable [#boutonNon];
  • line 46: [viewChild] (example 13) returns the element marked [#boutonNon] as a signal: it is equal to [undefined] as long as the window is closed;
  • line 50: an effect that depends on this signal: each time the window is opened, the “No” button appears, the signal changes, and the button receives focus. We chose “No,” the least dangerous response: pressing the Enter key by mistake does not delete anything.

docs.title: 3.7.3. Usage
docs.text:
// =========================================================================
// 16-confirmation/src/app/app.ts - use the confirmation window
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Same page as Example 21 from the NestJS course (links, buttons, confirmation),
// but without any round trips to a server.
// =========================================================================

import { Component, inject, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { ConfirmationService } from './confirmation/confirmation.service';
import { FenetreConfirmation } from './confirmation/fenetre-confirmation';

interface Contact {
  id: number;
  nom: string;
}

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  imports: [FenetreConfirmation],
  templateUrl: './app.html',
})
export class App {
  private readonly confirmation = inject(ConfirmationService);
  protected readonly contacts = signal<Contact[]>([
    { id: 1, nom: 'Jean MARTIN' },
    { id: 2, nom: 'Alice DURAND' },
    { id: 3, nom: 'Luc GERMAN' },
  ]);
  protected readonly message = signal('');

   // An async method: it “waits” for the user’s response
  protected async supprimer(c: Contact): Promise<void> {
    if (!(await this.confirmation.confirmer(`Supprimer le contact ${c.nom} ?`))) {
      this.message.set('Suppression abandonnée.');
      return;
    }
    this.contacts.update((liste) => liste.filter((x) => x.id !== c.id));
    this.message.set(`${c.nom} a été supprimé.`);
  }

  protected async toutSupprimer(): Promise<void> {
    if (await this.confirmation.confirmer(`Supprimer les ${this.contacts().length} contacts ?`)) {
      this.contacts.set([]);
      this.message.set('Tous les contacts ont été supprimés.');
    }
  }
}
  • line 19: the root component imports the window, which it will place in its template;
  • line 23: it requests the service;
  • lines 32–39: a method named [async]. On line 33, [await] suspends execution until the user responds; during this time, the application remains active. The rest of the method executes only if the response is “Yes”;
  • lines 41–46: same principle applies to deleting all contacts.
<div class="container py-4" style="max-width: 640px">
  <h1 class="h3 mb-3">Exemple 16 - une fenêtre de confirmation</h1>
  <ul class="list-group mb-3">
    @for (c of contacts(); track c.id) {
      <li class="list-group-item d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center">
        {{ c.nom }}
        <button class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger" (click)="supprimer(c)">Supprimer</button>
      </li>
    } @empty {
      <li class="list-group-item text-muted">Aucun contact.</li>
    }
  </ul>
  <button class="btn btn-danger" [disabled]="contacts().length === 0" (click)="toutSupprimer()">Tout supprimer</button>
  @if (message()) {
    <p class="alert alert-info mt-3">{{ message() }}</p>
  }
</div>
<!-- the window, UNE once for the entire application -->
<app-fenetre-confirmation />
  • lines 4–11: [@for] may be followed by a [@empty] block, displayed when the list is empty;
  • line 13: the button is disabled when there is nothing left to delete;
  • line 19: the window, positioned once for the entire application. Any component can then open it simply by calling the service.

[npm start 16-confirmation]; click the [Supprimer] button from Luc GERMAN:

With [Vue.js], the window and its state were provided by a “composable”; with [Angular], it’s a service. The principle is the same: a shared state, in a signal, that multiple components read and modify.

docs.title: 7. The RdvMedecins server, a black box
docs.text:
Examples 22 through 25, followed by the case study, interact with a server: the JSON server of the [RdvMedecins] application. This is the [NestJS] server from the previous lesson, whose controllers no longer generate HTML pages but instead produce JSON responses. Its business and data access layers remain unchanged.

In this course, this server is a black box: we don’t need to know how it’s written. All that matters is its API—that is, the list of HTTP requests it accepts and the responses it returns. This is the typical situation for a client developer: the API is a contract, and the server team can change whatever they want behind that contract. Its source code is provided ([rdvmedecins-nestjs-json] folder) and extensively commented, for the curious reader.

This chapter explains how to install the server, describes its API, and queries it using [curl].

docs.title: 7.1. The RdvMedecins Application
docs.text:
The application manages appointments for a medical practice. It has three roles:

RoleWhoWhat they can do[ADMIN]The administrator ([admin])Schedule and cancel appointments for all patients; manage doctors and clients[DOCTOR]Doctors ([pelissier], [tatou], [dupont])Schedule and cancel appointments for all patients; view all names in the calendars[USER]patients ([martin], [durand], [bistrou], [german])book appointments for themselves; cancel their appointments; manage their accounts. In the calendar, they cannot see the names of other patients

Demo accounts use their login as the password. The management rules are verified by the server, regardless of the client:

  • no appointments in the past;
  • only one upcoming appointment per patient;
  • a time slot can only be booked once per day;
  • two doctors (or two clients) cannot have the same first and last names; a login belongs to only one account;
  • a doctor with appointments cannot be deleted;
  • A record that has been modified in the meantime by someone else cannot be overwritten (optimistic lock);
  • a patient is never assigned the name of another patient.

docs.title: 7.2. Installation
docs.text:
You will need [Node.js] and a [MySQL] (or [MariaDB]) server: their installation is described in the appendix.

1. The database. The script [database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql] creates the database [dbrdvmedecins2], its tables, and its sample data. Using [Laragon], run it from within [HeidiSQL] (File menu / Run a SQL file); at the command line:

mysql -u root -p < database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql

The script always starts with an empty database: you can rerun it to restore the initial data.

2. Libraries. In a console window open to the [rdvmedecins-nestjs-json] folder:

npm install

3. Configuration. Copy the file [.env.example] to [.env] (under [Windows]: [copy .env.example .env]), then modify it:

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sample configuration file.
# Copy this file to [.env], then adjust the values for your machine.
# The [.env] file must never be shared or committed (passwords).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------

# listening port for the JSON server (the Angular client connects to it via the ng-serve proxy)
PORT=8080

# Database connection parameters for MySQL [dbrdvmedecins2]
# (script: database/dbrdvmedecins2.sql)
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=3306
DB_USERNAME=root
DB_PASSWORD=
DB_DATABASE=dbrdvmedecins2
# true: displays in the console the SQL queries sent to MySQL
DB_LOGGING=false

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# authentication
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# secret key used to sign/verify JWT tokens—must be changed
# must be used in production (a long random string, never committed).
JWT_SECRET=change-moi-en-une-longue-chaine-aleatoire
# validity period of a JWT token, in seconds (7200 s = 2 h). The cookie
# that carries the token has the same lifetime.
JWT_EXPIRES_IN_SECONDS=7200
# Set to true in production (site served as HTTPS): the
# will then never be sent over an unencrypted connection.
COOKIE_SECURE=false

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# bot protection
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# login: number of failed attempts (incorrect CAPTCHA or password) allowed for
# the same login from the same address IP, before this combination is blocked...
LOGIN_MAX_ECHECS=5
# ... during this period (an address IP is also blocked if it accumulates
# 5 times as many failed attempts, across all logins)
LOGIN_BLOCAGE_MINUTES=15
# customer account creation: maximum number of accounts created per hour
# from the same IP address. In a classroom, all workstations log out
# from the same IP address: increase if necessary.
INSCRIPTION_MAX_PAR_HEURE=10

# MODE TEST captcha: if this variable has a value, that value is
# accepted as the answer to the N'IMPORTE QUEL CAPTCHA. Useful for querying
# the API using curl (you can’t “read” the image in a console).
# Leave VIDE in production.
CAPTCHA_TEST=

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# production
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Compiled Angular client folder, served by this server (default: client/)
# DOSSIER_CLIENT=client
# Set to true if the server is behind a proxy (nginx...)
TRUST_PROXY=false
  • line 8: the server listens on port 8080;
  • lines 12–16: the connection to [MySQL]. With [Laragon], the user [root] has no password: the default values are fine;
  • line 25: the secret key that signs the authentication tokens;
  • lines 38–45: anti-bot protections (lockout after multiple failed login attempts, number of accounts created per hour);
  • line 51: the CAPTCHA test mode. The login page requires users to retype the characters from an image, which is impossible from a console. If this variable has a value, that value is accepted as the answer to any CAPTCHA, similar to the “test keys” that [Google] provides for its [reCAPTCHA]. For the tests with [curl] in this chapter, enter [CAPTCHA_TEST=test]. Leave it as VIDE in production;
  • lines 57–59: two settings for production (see the “Deployment” chapter).

4. Launch.

npm run start:dev

The console displays (excerpt):

[Nest] LOG [NestFactory] Starting Nest application...
[Nest] LOG [RoutesResolver] AgendaController {/api/agenda}:
[Nest] LOG [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/api/agenda, GET} route
[Nest] LOG [RoutesResolver] RendezVousController {/api/rendez-vous}:
...
[Nest] WARN [RdvMedecins] MODE TEST du captcha actif (CAPTCHA_TEST dans .env) : à ne jamais utiliser en production
[Nest] LOG [NestApplication] Nest application successfully started
[Nest] LOG [RdvMedecins] serveur JSON démarré : http://localhost:8080/api

If the database is inaccessible ([MySQL] server stopped, incorrect password), the server stops immediately with a connection error message.

docs.title: 7.3. Response Format
docs.text:
All URLs begin with [/api]. A successful request receives a 2xx status code and, in its body, the requested data in the format JSON. A rejected request receives a 4xx or 5xx status code and, in the body, data in the same format:

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "cle": "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM",
  "params": { "min": "6" },
  "champs": { "nom": "ERRORS.LASTNAME_REQUIRED", "password": "ERRORS.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT" }
}
  • [statusCode]: the code HTTP, repeated in the body;
  • [cle]: the message translation key. The server never returns text to be displayed: it no longer knows the user’s language. It is the client that translates the key using its dictionaries (see Example 21);
  • [params] (optional): message parameters ([Au moins {min} caractères], [Réessayez dans {minutes} minute(s)]);
  • [champs] (optional): for a rejected form, the error for each field.

Codes used:

CodeMeaningExamples of keys400Invalid request[ERRORS.INVALID_FORM] (+ fields), [ERRORS.INVALID_DATE], [ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA], [ERRORS.CHOOSE_PATIENT], [ERRORS.WRONG_CURRENT_PASSWORD], [ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST]...401not authenticated[ERRORS.AUTH_REQUIRED] (no token), [ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED] (invalid or expired token), [LOGIN.ERROR]403Access Denied[ERRORS.FORBIDDEN] (insufficient role), [ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT] (no pass)404Not found[ERRORS.NOT_FOUND], [ERRORS.DOCTOR_NOT_FOUND], [ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND]...409Business rule violation[ERRORS.PAST_DATE], [ERRORS.SLOT_ALREADY_BOOKED], [ERRORS.LOGIN_TAKEN], [ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE]...415POST, which is not in JSON[ERRORS.JSON_REQUIRED]429Too many attempts[ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS], [ERRORS.TOO_MANY_ACCOUNTS] (+ params.minutes)500server error[ERRORS.SERVER_ERROR]

docs.title: 7.4. Authentication
docs.text:
The client authenticates using [POST /api/auth/login], with a username, password, and CAPTCHA response. In return, the server places a cookie in the browser that contains a signed token JWT:

Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...; Max-Age=7200; Path=/api; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict

Its attributes are important for security:

  • [HttpOnly]: The page’s [JavaScript] code cannot read this cookie. A malicious script injected into the page would therefore be unable to steal the token. Consequence for the client: it cannot determine on its own whether it is logged in. It asks the server ([GET /api/auth/moi]);
  • [Path=/api]: the browser only includes it in requests to API;
  • [SameSite=Strict]: The browser only includes this token in requests sent to DEPUIS for a page on this site. A malicious page on another site cannot cause the browser to act on the user’s behalf (a so-called CSRF attack);
  • [Max-Age=7200]: It expires after two hours, at the same time the token expires.

The browser then automatically sends this cookie with every request to [/api]. The client [Angular] therefore does not need to do anything to authenticate itself, provided that its pages and API share the same origin (same protocol, same machine, same port). This is the role of the proxy on the [Angular] development server (see Example 22), and of the server itself in production (see the “Deployment” chapter).

A second safeguard against CSRF attacks: the server rejects (415) any POST request whose body is not in JSON. A compromised HTML form on another site cannot send JSON.

docs.title: 7.5. The API
docs.text:
MethodAddressRolesSent/response bodyGET[/api/captcha]publicResponse: [{ id, svg }]POST[/api/auth/login]public[{ login, password, captchaId, captcha }]; response: [{ login, nom, role }] + cookiePOST[/api/auth/logout]public[{}]; deletes the cookieGET[/api/auth/moi]logged inresponse: [{ login, nom, role }]GET[/api/agenda?idMedecin=&jour=]allAnswer: the calendar (excluding idMedecin: for a DOCTOR, his own)POST[/api/rendez-vous]all[{ jour, idCreneau, idClient }] (idClient ignored for a USER); 201DELETE[/api/rendez-vous/:id]allA USER cancels only its ownGET[/api/medecins]allthe list (with login for ADMIN)GET[/api/clients]ADMIN, DOCTORthe list (with login for ADMIN)GET[/api/medecins/:id], [/api/clients/:id]ADMINa recordPOST[/api/medecins], [/api/clients]ADMIN[{ titre, prenom, nom, login?, password? }]; 201PUT[/api/medecins/:id], [/api/clients/:id]ADMIN[{ titre, prenom, nom, login?, password?, version }]DELETE[/api/medecins/:id], [/api/clients/:id]ADMINResponse: [{}]POST[/api/inscription/acces]public[{ captchaId, captcha }]; issues a token (cookie)GET[/api/inscription/acces]publicresponse: [{ valide }]POST[/api/inscription]public + pass[{ titre, prenom, nom, login, password, confirmation }]; 201GET[/api/mon-espace]USERResponse: [{ patient, rendezVous }]GET[/api/mon-compte]USERResponse: [{ titre, prenom, nom, login, version }]PUT[/api/mon-compte]USER[{ titre, prenom, nom, login, password?, confirmation?, motDePasseActuel, version }]DELETE[/api/mon-compte]USER[{ motDePasseActuel }]; deletes the account and its appointments

A calendar entry ([GET /api/agenda]) describes a time slot (ET) and what the logged-in user is authorized to do with it:

{ "id": 3, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 0,
  "libre": false,
  "patient": { "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Alice", "nom": "DURAND" },
  "moi": false, "reservable": false, "idRv": 2 }
  • [libre]: Is the time slot available on that day?
  • [patient]: the patient for the appointment. For a logged-in patient, this is equal to [null], except for SON appointments: the names of other patients are never sent;
  • [moi]: This is the logged-in patient’s appointment;
  • [reservable]: Can the user book this time slot (available, not in the past, and, for a patient, no upcoming appointments)?
  • [idRv]: Set if the user can cancel this appointment.

The server sets DÉCIDE; the client displays it. And even if a client were to cheat (by displaying a “Book” button when it shouldn’t), the server would double-check everything at the time of booking.

docs.title: 7.6. Query the API using curl
docs.text:
The [curl] folder on the server contains the JSON request bodies from this chapter, with one file per request. For example, [curl/login-admin.json]:

{ "login": "admin", "password": "admin", "captchaId": "-", "captcha": "test" }

Commands are entered in a console opened on the [rdvmedecins-nestjs-json] directory. Some options for [curl]:

  • [-i]: also display the response headers; [-s]: without a progress bar;
  • [--json @fichier]: send the contents of the file in POST, with the header [Content-Type: application/json] (curl 7.82 and later; with an older version, use [-H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @fichier]);
  • [-X PUT], [-X DELETE]: the HTTP method;
  • [-c cookies.txt]: save the received cookies to this file; [-b cookies.txt]: send them back. This is how [curl] “stays logged in” from one command to the next, just as a browser would.

Under [PowerShell], you must enter [curl.exe] and not [curl] (which refers to a different command there). The somewhat lengthy responses for JSON have been formatted for this document, and the headers for [Date], [ETag], [Connection], and [Keep-Alive] have been removed.

docs.title: 7.6.1. Login
docs.text:
First, the CAPTCHA (the image is cropped):

$ curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/captcha
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: no-store
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 11397

{"id": "9931064f-dcc3-45f7-a35c-3057d208a1d4", "svg": "<svg xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\" width=\"150..."}

Without a token, a protected URL returns a 401 response:

$ curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 47

{"statusCode": 401, "cle": "ERRORS.AUTH_REQUIRED"}

An incorrect CAPTCHA, followed by an incorrect password:

$ curl -i --json @curl/login-mauvais-captcha.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 91

{"statusCode": 400, "cle": "ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA", "champs": {"captcha": "ERRORS.WRONG_CAPTCHA"}}

$ curl -i --json @curl/login-mauvais-mdp.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 38

{"statusCode": 401, "cle": "LOGIN.ERROR"}

A successful login sets the cookie, which [curl] stores in [cookies.txt]:

$ curl -i -c cookies.txt --json @curl/login-admin.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...; Max-Age=7200; Path=/api; Expires=Mon, 28 Sep 2026 12:49:12 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"login": "admin", "nom": "Administrateur", "role": "ADMIN"}

With this cookie, the server knows who we are:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt http://localhost:8080/api/auth/me
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"login": "admin", "nom": "Administrateur", "role": "ADMIN"}

A forged (or expired) token results in an expired session, and the server instructs the browser to delete the cookie:

$ curl -i -b "rdvmedecins_jwt=abc.def.ghi" http://localhost:8080/api/auth/me
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=; Path=/api; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 49

{"statusCode": 401, "cle": "ERRORS.SESSION_EXPIRED"}

docs.title: 7.6.3. Appointments
docs.text:
ADMIN reserves slot 3 for patient No. 2 (Alice DURAND). The body of the request:

{ "jour": "2030-01-15", "idCreneau": 3, "idClient": 2 }

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/rv-admin.json http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"id": 2, "jour": "2030-01-15", "idCreneau": 3, "idClient": 2}

The calendar now displays this appointment, along with the patient’s name and instructions on how to cancel it ([idRv]):

$ curl -s -b cookies.txt "http://localhost:8080/api/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2030-01-15"
{
  "medecin": {"id": 1, "version": 0, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Marie", "nom": "PELISSIER"},
  "jour": "2030-01-15",
  "creneaux": [
    {"id": 1, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 8, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 2, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 8, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 3, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 0, "libre": false, "patient": {"titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Alice", "nom": "DURAND"}, "moi": false, "reservable": false, "idRv": 2},
    {"id": 4, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 5, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 6, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 7, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 8, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 9, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 10, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 11, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 12, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 12, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null}
  ],
  "info": null
}

Try again: the patient already has an upcoming appointment. An appointment in the past is also rejected:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/rv-admin.json http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 66

{"statusCode": 409, "cle": "ERRORS.PATIENT_HAS_UPCOMING_APPOINTMENT"}

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/rv-passe.json http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 43

{"statusCode": 409, "cle": "ERRORS.PAST_DATE"}

A standard HTML form (simulated here by [-d], which sends [application/x-www-form-urlencoded]) is rejected:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -d "jour=2030-01-15&idCreneau=4&idClient=2" http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 415 Unsupported Media Type
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 47

{"statusCode": 415, "cle": "ERRORS.JSON_REQUIRED"}

docs.title: 7.6.4. A patient’s perspective
docs.text:
You log out, then log in as [martin]:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -c cookies.txt --json @curl/vide.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/logout
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=; Path=/api; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

$ curl -s -c cookies-martin.txt --json @curl/login-martin.json http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login
{"login": "martin", "nom": "Jean MARTIN", "role": "USER"}

The same schedule, as seen by a patient: Slot 3 is taken (["libre": false]), but ["patient"] is equivalent to [null]: Alice's name, DURAND, was not sent:

$ curl -s -b cookies-martin.txt "http://localhost:8080/api/agenda?idMedecin=1&jour=2030-01-15"
{
  "medecin": {"id": 1, "version": 0, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Marie", "nom": "PELISSIER"},
  "jour": "2030-01-15",
  "creneaux": [
    {"id": 1, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 8, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 2, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 8, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 3, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 0, "libre": false, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": false, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 4, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 5, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 6, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 7, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 8, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 9, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 10, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 11, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 12, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 12, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null}
  ],
  "info": null
}

A patient does not have access to the client list:

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt http://localhost:8080/api/clients
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 43

{"statusCode": 403, "cle": "ERRORS.FORBIDDEN"}

They are making a reservation for themselves (the body does not contain [idClient]), once, not twice:

{ "jour": "2030-01-15", "idCreneau": 5 }

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt --json @curl/rv-martin.json http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"id": 3, "jour": "2030-01-15", "idCreneau": 5, "idClient": 1}

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt --json @curl/rv-martin-2.json http://localhost:8080/api/appointments
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 53

{"statusCode": 409, "cle": "AGENDA.ALREADY_BOOKED_INFO"}

His space:

$ curl -s -b cookies-martin.txt http://localhost:8080/api/my-space
{
  "patient": {"titre": "Mr", "prenom": "Jean", "nom": "MARTIN"},
  "rendezVous": [
    {
      "id": 3,
      "jour": "2030-01-15",
      "creneau": {"id": 5, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 40},
      "medecin": {"id": 1, "version": 0, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Marie", "nom": "PELISSIER"}
    }
  ]
}

He cannot cancel another patient’s appointment. The server responds with “not found,” just as it would for an appointment that doesn’t exist: it reveals nothing about other patients’ appointments:

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/appointments/2
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 55

{"statusCode": 404, "cle": "ERRORS.APPOINTMENT_NOT_FOUND"}

His own, yes:

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/appointments/3
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

docs.title: 7.6.5. A doctor’s perspective
docs.text:
Without [idMedecin], a logged-in doctor receives the SON calendar, with all the names:

$ curl -s -b cookies-pelissier.txt "http://localhost:8080/api/agenda?jour=2030-01-15"
{
  "medecin": {"id": 1, "version": 0, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Marie", "nom": "PELISSIER"},
  "jour": "2030-01-15",
  "creneaux": [
    {"id": 1, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 8, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 2, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 8, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 3, "hdebut": 8, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 0, "libre": false, "patient": {"titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Alice", "nom": "DURAND"}, "moi": false, "reservable": false, "idRv": 2},
    {"id": 4, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 5, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 9, "mfin": 40, "libre": false, "patient": {"titre": "Mr", "prenom": "Jean", "nom": "MARTIN"}, "moi": false, "reservable": false, "idRv": 3},
    {"id": 6, "hdebut": 9, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 7, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 8, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 10, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 9, "hdebut": 10, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 10, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 0, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 20, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 11, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 20, "hfin": 11, "mfin": 40, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null},
    {"id": 12, "hdebut": 11, "mdebut": 40, "hfin": 12, "mfin": 0, "libre": true, "patient": null, "moi": false, "reservable": true, "idRv": null}
  ],
  "info": null
}

It does not manage doctors:

$ curl -i -b cookies-pelissier.txt --json @curl/medecin-ajout.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 43

{"statusCode": 403, "cle": "ERRORS.FORBIDDEN"}

docs.title: 7.6.6. Managing doctors and clients (ADMIN)
docs.text:
An addition. If the username is missing, the default is the name in lowercase; the password is the username:

{ "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Claire", "nom": "LEROY" }

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/medecin-ajout.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 82

{"id": 4, "version": 1, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Claire", "nom": "LEROY", "login": "leroy"}

Invalid body: the response lists the error for each field:

{ "titre": "Dr", "prenom": "", "nom": "UN-NOM-BIEN-TROP-LONG-POUR-LA-BASE", "login": "Claire L" }

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/medecin-invalide.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 210

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "cle": "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM",
  "params": {"min": "6"},
  "champs": {"login": "ERRORS.INVALID_LOGIN", "titre": "ERRORS.INVALID_TITLE", "prenom": "ERRORS.FIRSTNAME_REQUIRED", "nom": "ERRORS.LASTNAME_TOO_LONG"}
}

A homonym: both affected fields are flagged:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt --json @curl/medecin-doublon.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 143

{"statusCode": 409, "cle": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS", "champs": {"prenom": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS", "nom": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_ALREADY_EXISTS"}}

A modification. The [version] is the one read from the record (here, 1):

{ "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Claire", "nom": "LEROY-MARTIN", "version": 1 }

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X PUT --json @curl/medecin-modif.json http://localhost:8080/api/doctors/4
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 89

{"id": 4, "version": 2, "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Claire", "nom": "LEROY-MARTIN", "login": "leroy"}

The record is now at version 2. Resubmitting the same change (with version 1) would overwrite a record that has since been modified by someone else: the optimistic lock prevents this:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X PUT --json @curl/medecin-modif.json http://localhost:8080/api/medecins/4
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 51

{"statusCode": 409, "cle": "ERRORS.CONCURRENT_UPDATE"}

A doctor with appointments cannot be deleted; the others can:

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/doctors/1
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 57

{"statusCode": 409, "cle": "ERRORS.DOCTOR_HAS_APPOINTMENTS"}

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -X DELETE http://localhost:8080/api/doctors/4
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

docs.title: 7.6.7. Creating an account
docs.text:
Without a pass, it’s impossible:

$ curl -i --json @curl/inscription.json http://localhost:8080/api/registration
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 56

{"statusCode": 403, "cle": "ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT"}

First, you solve a CAPTCHA; the server issues a token, valid for 15 minutes, in a cookie:

$ curl -i -c cookies-inscription.txt --json @curl/captcha-test.json http://localhost:8080/api/registration/access
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_inscription=1c3352aa-26ba-4f85-9f61-ed2c6a731d84; Max-Age=900; Path=/api/inscription; Expires=Mon, 28 Sep 2026 11:04:12 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

$ curl -s -b cookies-inscription.txt http://localhost:8080/api/registration/access
{"valide": true}

The password confirmation must be identical:

$ curl -i -b cookies-inscription.txt --json @curl/inscription-confirmation.json http://localhost:8080/api/registration
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 98

{"statusCode": 400, "cle": "ERRORS.INVALID_FORM", "champs": {"confirmation": "ERRORS.PASSWORDS_DIFFER"}}

{ "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Julie", "nom": "BERNARD", "login": "jbernard", "password": "secret1", "confirmation": "secret1" }

$ curl -i -b cookies-inscription.txt -c cookies-inscription.txt --json @curl/inscription.json http://localhost:8080/api/registration
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_inscription=; Path=/api/inscription; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 20

{"login": "jbernard"}

The passcode has been used: it cannot be used to create a second account:

$ curl -i -b cookies-inscription.txt --json @curl/inscription.json http://localhost:8080/api/registration
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 56

{"statusCode": 403, "cle": "ERRORS.CAPTCHA_BEFORE_ACCOUNT"}

docs.title: 7.6.8. Manage Your Account
docs.text:
The new patient logs in and reads her medical record:

$ curl -s -b cookies-jbernard.txt http://localhost:8080/api/my-account
{"titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Julie", "nom": "BERNARD", "login": "jbernard", "version": 1}

Making a change requires the current password. The server issues a new token, which contains the new name:

{ "titre": "Mme", "prenom": "Julie", "nom": "BERNARD-DUVAL", "login": "jbernard", "motDePasseActuel": "secret1", "version": 1 }

$ curl -i -b cookies-jbernard.txt -c cookies-jbernard.txt -X PUT --json @curl/mon-compte.json http://localhost:8080/api/my-account
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...; Max-Age=7200; Path=/api; Expires=Mon, 28 Sep 2026 12:49:13 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 62

{"login": "jbernard", "nom": "Julie BERNARD-DUVAL", "role": "USER"}

Deleting the account also deletes the cookie:

$ curl -i -b cookies-jbernard.txt -c cookies-jbernard.txt -X DELETE --json @curl/mon-compte-suppression.json http://localhost:8080/api/my-account
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rdvmedecins_jwt=; Path=/api; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 2

{}

$ curl -i -b cookies-jbernard.txt http://localhost:8080/api/auth/me
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 47

{"statusCode": 401, "cle": "ERRORS.AUTH_REQUIRED"}

docs.title: 7.6.9. Some errors
docs.text:
An unknown route, a body that is not a valid JSON:

$ curl -i -b cookies-martin.txt http://localhost:8080/api/does-not-exist
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 43

{"statusCode": 404, "cle": "ERRORS.NOT_FOUND"}

$ curl -i -b cookies.txt -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{pas du json" http://localhost:8080/api/appointment
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: 45

{"statusCode": 400, "cle": "ERRORS.BAD_REQUEST"}

We now know everything we need to know about the server to write our client.
